But he added: "I'm struggling and the winter is hard, but painting the mill has attracted more visitors here and helped me pay the bills."

He is gathering the opinions of visitors to the mill this summer to make a case to the council.

News.title: British couple held in Iran end hunger strike
News.content:
A British couple jailed in Iran after being accused of espionage have ended their hunger strikes after 93 and 84 days respectively.

Craig and Lindsay Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while passing through Iran on a motorcycle journey from Europe to Australia. They were both sentenced to 10 years in jail in February, but Craig Foreman's family said his punishment had been extended by two years after speaking to the media.

The couple from East Sussex, who both deny espionage, went on hunger strike in May when prison authorities prevented them from calling their families.

The family of the couple said they had been protesting against how they and other prisoners were being treated.

A spokesperson for the family said the couple agreed with prison guards to end their strike to be able to speak directly to their loved ones again.

However, the family said contact was yet to be re-established, as of Monday afternoon.

The family had also previously called for the couple to end their hunger strike.

Five people outside the prison joined the pair on their hunger strike for the final five days from Tuesday to Saturday as an act of solidarity, the family added.

Lindsay Foreman's son Joe Bennett and four unnamed others took part in the UK, as well as other prisoners inside Tehran's Evin jail, the family said.

"My mum and Craig have spent months on hunger strike, and even at the point of bringing it to an end they wanted to make it about something bigger than themselves," Bennett, from Folkestone in Kent, said.

"Those final five days became about people standing together around values that should be universal: Truth, justice, kindness, peace and unity."

By the end of the protest, Craig Foreman had been on hunger strike for 93 days, and Lindsay Foreman for 84 days, the family added.

Although they said they were unaware of the condition of the pair, who had consumed just milk and either honey or salt in water during their strikes.

Bennett said the couple also went on a separate hunger strike back in November as a "cry out for help".

Explosive video footage purportedly shows the moment a Ukrainian drone destroyed a Russian military vehicle used to coordinate vital air defences.

Ukraine’s ‘Black Forest’ Reconnaissance Brigade claimed to have struck what it said was the command-and-staff vehicle for a Soviet-era S-300 surface-to-air missile system.

Video published on Sunday showed the moment of impact from above as a loitering drone hit the side of the truck with devastating effect, sending smoke billowing from the wreckage.

open image in gallery The moment of impact in footage shared on Sunday from an undisclosed location ( 15th Artillery Reconnaissance Brigade / YouTube )

In a social media post, the brigade said it would have been a “very painful blow” to the Russian forces, and destroying it would allow Ukrainian vehicles to fly deeper into Russia to hit strategic targets.

It added: “They are also stuffed with rare electronics, are damn expensive, and it takes years to train the crew. An approach on such a target is a very painful blow for the enemy.”

The Russian vehicle appeared to be a 5K76 command-and-control vehicle, or its more modern 5K76M variant, according to Ukraine’s official fundraising platform United24.

open image in gallery A huge orange explosion from the truck at the moment of impact ( 15th Artillery Reconnaissance Brigade / YouTube )

The 5K76 serves as a mobile command centre for the S-300, also known by its Nato reporting name SA-10 Grumble.

The S-300s were a family of surface-to-air missile systems developed by Russia, then the Soviet Union, in the late 1970s and can fire missiles at incoming targets up to 40 kilometres from the command centre.

Use peaked in 2000 as Russia fielded around 1,900 launchers. That had dropped to about 800 by 2017, according to the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. Some were sent to Crimea after 2014.

There is no publicly available cost estimate for the 5K76.

open image in gallery A Russian surface-to-air missile system S-300 in 2012 (file) ( AFP/Getty )

The US and Ukraine are separately reported to be working on modernising the Ukrainian S-300 air defence systems as Russia steps up its attacks on residential hubs nationwide.

Kyiv has repeatedly asked Western allies for more air defences to protect critical infrastructure and civilian areas from frequent Russian missile and drone attacks.

In highest demand are the American Patriot interceptors, key to defending against a nightly barrage of Russian ballistic missile strikes.

But the Iran war has drained arsenals in the US and the Gulf, and some European countries are holding onto missiles they may need for their own defence.

Col. Robert Hamilton (Ret.) told PBS last week: “There's a joint US-Ukrainian effort going on to essentially retrofit or upgrade the old S-300 missiles or a newer variant of the S-300 and give it better capabilities.

open image in gallery An illustration of the command vehicle for the S-300 SAM system ( 15th Artillery Reconnaissance Brigade / YouTube )

“And so that should come online near the end of this year. But, again, we're talking 100 or a couple of hundred a year that could be produced.”

He said those variants could “help fill this Patriot gap”.

US president Donald Trump offered Ukraine the right to make its own Patriot interceptors in July, but later reneged, saying the US has “not agreed” to such an arrangement.

Russia has tried to deter the US from giving Ukraine the means to defend itself, warning that donating interceptors would amount to a direct escalation. Moscow has said it would delay the chance of peace.

The U.S.’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to its lowest point since the 1980s, according to new data from the Energy Department.

The SPR was at 298.7 million barrels as of Friday, according to the department.

The last time the reserve dropped below the 300 million barrel mark was in the early 1980s, when the U.S. was rapidly increasing its reserve storage in response to an oil embargo on the U.S. put in place by Arab members of OPEC in the 1970s.

The Trump administration forecast the drop when it announced in March that it planned to release 182 million barrels from the reserve over the course of 120 days. The release was authorized as disruptions to the oil market were expected due to President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, which began at the end of February.

The war has caused gas prices to explode over the last several months, with no sign of significant reductions on the horizon.

Oil storage tanks at the Sunoco LP Fuel Supply Terminal in Austin, Texas. Oil held in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to its lowest levels since 1983 ( Getty )

It's not the first time in recent history that the federal government has released oil from the reserve. In 2022, President Joe Biden authorized the release of 180 million barrels after Russia invaded Ukraine. The invasion spiked oil prices worldwide.

Patrick De Haan, the head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, said in an X post that declines in the SPR were likely going to continue "for a few more weeks before the authorized release is complete."

An Energy Department spokesperson told CNBC in July that the minimum amount of oil needed to safely operate the SPR is approximately 70 million barrels.

David Goldwyn, who served as a State Department special envoy for international energy affairs during former President Barack Obama's administration, said he was not concerned that the oil reserves were under threat of depletion.

“I’m not worried about the stability of the reserve or our ability to do another drawdown, if we needed to,” he said at the time.

Prior to the U.S. and Israel's war in Iran, the SPR contained approximately 415 million barrels of oil.

The SPR's ability to operate is reportedly at risk from its aging infrastructure, according to a report released in May from the Government Accountability Office.

More than quarter of the SPR's oil inventory is reportedly "not available for drawdown due to a combination of construction outages and cavern outages," as of December 2025, the agency determined.

That means that a portion of the oil in the reserve — a minimum of 103 million barrels, according to a Rapidan Energy analysis published in July — can't be accessed at the moment.

“The SPR’s drawdown, distribution and fill capabilities are currently limited and are at risk going forward due to longstanding issues with aging infrastructure compounded with ongoing major construction intended to address them,” the GAO said in its report.

Meanwhile, U.S. oil prices have continued to climb as confidence that Washington can reach a deal with Tehran ending the war dwindles.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices rose 5.1 percent to $82.13 on Monday, while Brent Crude — a global benchmark for oil prices — jumped 5 percent to $87.72 per barrel the same day, the New York Post reports.

The jump came after Trump told Axios on Sunday that the U.S. is only "semi-negotiating" with Iran.

“We are low-keying it,” he said. We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

On Monday, the national average for gas was $4.0091 per gallon, according to AAA. That price is down slightly from yesterday when the national average was at $4.0121, but still far higher than a month ago, when the national average was $3.8835 and a year ago when it was $3.1394.

A speedboat operator has been charged in federal court with misconduct and neglect after a vessel capsized near the Statue of Liberty, killing a 27-year-old mother and her infant daughter.

Manuel Hernandez, 46, of Manville, New Jersey, wiped away tears during his initial appearance in Manhattan federal court on Monday, where he appeared in ankle shackles. He was released on $50,000 bail without entering a plea.

Sara Sanchez and her 5-month-old daughter, Antonella Garcia, died after the 22-foot Yamaha AR210 speedboat overturned in New York Harbor late Saturday.

Authorities attributed the disaster to an overcrowded boat, improper decision-making by Hernandez, a lack of required commercial licenses, and the failure to secure a life jacket on the infant. Twelve other individuals were rescued and remain in stable condition.

Following the hearing, court-appointed attorney Amy Gallicchio guided Hernandez to a waiting vehicle, with both declining to offer comment.

The vessel was retrieved from the water and transported to the New York Police Department’s harbor unit facility on Randall’s Island.

Although state charges were initially lodged over the weekend, prosecutors announced Monday that Hernandez will face trial in federal court. He was transferred into federal custody on Sunday.

( Getty )

A federal criminal complaint levels two charges against Hernandez, alleging that as the operator, his negligent actions and omissions led to the capsizing and fatalities. Prosecutors noted the boat carried 14 people, exceeding its maximum limit of 10.

Officials further stated that he knowingly operated the boat with an infant aboard despite being aware that no infant- or child-sized life jackets were present.

The evening charter began at 7 p.m. Saturday and was more than three hours underway when Hernandez steered the boat toward the Statue of Liberty and executed a U-turn into a swell, likely created by the wake of a larger passing vessel, according to court documents.

In an attempt to maneuver past the swell, Hernandez accelerated, causing water to swamp the bow and immediately capsize the vessel, prosecutors wrote.

Hernandez informed investigators that he had worked for the charter firm on a freelance or contract basis since last year, starting out as a limousine driver.

He acknowledged using his personal boat, a slightly larger Yamaha AR250, twice recently for tours organized through Zeus Luxury Rentals Inc., according to the filing.

On Saturday, however, he borrowed a friend’s boat because his own was undergoing repairs, omitting to tell the owner that he intended to use it for a commercial tour, court records state.

Hernandez admitted to investigators that he had never obtained the required licensing, claiming he was unaware it was needed.

He also acknowledged proceeding with the excursion involving the 5-month-old infant despite knowing the vessel lacked child-sized life vests.

Police Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch said the "tragedy could have been prevented, and now a family is left to grieve the unimaginable loss of a mother and her 5-month-old daughter because of his negligence."

U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald stated in a press release that Hernandez disregarded federal regulations and maritime safety standards by carrying paying passengers on a commercial trip without the necessary licenses.

"We mourn the tragic drowning deaths of the infant and her mother and urge would-be tour operators and the public to observe all safety protocols for commercial vessels," he added.

Capt. Doreen McCarthy, the Coast Guard Sector New York commander, credited the rescue of the surviving passengers to "heroic, swift actions" by multi-agency responders and a good Samaritan vessel.

Meanwhile, an online fundraiser established Sunday to help partner Andres Garcia pay for funeral and living costs for Sanchez and their daughter had surpassed $25,000 by Tuesday afternoon.

Garcia was also aboard the vessel when it overturned.

Antonio Russo, general manager at Il Punto Ristorante, called Garcia an "amazing guy" who worked extensive hours weekly as a driver, waiter, and food-runner to support his family in New York and Colombia.

Diego Naranjo, a Queens neighbor of Sanchez, recalled first meeting her last spring when her young son accidentally threw a ball into his yard, leading to an invitation for him to play on a trampoline with Naranjo's children.

"They were really nice people. You can see when a person is noble," Naranjo said, adding that he was deeply shocked after having just seen Sanchez bringing groceries home last Tuesday.

President Donald Trump appeared to zone out during an Oval Office announcement on vaccines, prompting a fresh round of mockery online.

On Monday, Trump signed an executive order that calls for reducing the number of vaccines recommended for children and splitting the MMR shot — which protects against measles, mumps and rubella — into three individual vaccines.

The order is the latest step in the administration’s campaign to remake the childhood vaccination schedule, led by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has long questioned vaccine safety.

During the ceremony, the 80-year-old president appeared to repeatedly close his eyes while seated behind the Resolute Desk — including as Kennedy and National Institutes of Health Director Jay Bhattacharya spoke beside him.

Videos of the moments quickly circulated on social media.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump appeared to zone out during a vaccine announcement in the Oval Office on Monday with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr ( AFP via Getty Images )

“I love how he pops out of it for a few seconds then closes his eyes again and he's right back in dream land. This is getting ridiculous,” wrote one X user. Another chimed in: “Why doesn't the assembled media speak out about this...they all see it.”

“What a loser,” a third user wrote. “After years of listening to those ‘sleepy joe’ comments…” The remark referred to Trump’s longtime nickname for former President Joe Biden, whom he repeatedly accused of being mentally and physically unfit for office.

Some commenters, however, were more supportive of the president. “In Trump's defense, good Lord, the speaker is boring,” one wrote.

Trump, the oldest person ever inaugurated as president, has faced persistent scrutiny over his health since returning to the White House, including over moments during official events in which he has appeared to close his eyes for extended periods. One such moment came during Lindsey Graham’s funeral last month.

“The president has severe daytime somnolence,” CNN medical analyst Dr. Jonathan Reiner said in May. “He falls asleep very often. He’s fallen asleep in the Oval Office on multiple occasions with people talking to him, in the cabinet room,” he said. “And chronic insomnia is a severe illness. It can result in an increase in risk of dementia, a decrease in cognitive effects in older people.”

open image in gallery Director of the National Institutes of Health Jay Bhattacharya (L) speaks before President Donald Trump signs an executive order calling for more research and flexibility on vaccines ( AFP via Getty Images )

The White House, meanwhile, has forcefully rejected such claims.

“President Trump is the sharpest, most accessible, and energetic president in American history and any so-called medical professionals engaging in armchair diagnosis or false speculation for political purposes are clearly breaking the Hippocratic Oath they’ve sworn to,” a White House spokesperson told The Independent at the time.

Trump, for his part, has repeatedly insisted that he is in excellent health. After a physical at Walter Reed in May, the president wrote on Truth Social that “everything” had “checked out PERFECTLY.”

In a YouGov survey conducted last year, 78 percent of respondents said they believed Trump had not been transparent about his physical health.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

Councils will be given greater powers to block betting shops and vape stores under government plans to revitalise Britain’s "hollowed-out high streets".

Andy Burnham plans to abolish the so-called "aim to permit" rule, first introduced by Sir Tony Blair, which limits the ability of town halls to refuse licences to gambling premises and venues with round-the-clock slot machines.

Vape shops will also face tighter controls, with new stores required to see planning approval from next year. The legal definition of a vape store will also be tightened to prevent retailers trying to bypass regulations by describing themselves as a "convenience store”.

open image in gallery A man cycles past a William Hill bookmakers on Deptford High Street, London. Councils are set to have greater powers to reject new applications for bookmakers ( Getty )

Similarly, centres which operate 24-hour slot and fruit machines will also require planning consent under the changes.

The measures are part of a package designed to halt the decline of Britain’s high streets - and even make them look better. New expectations on the design of shop fronts will tackle “garish neon signs” and oversized logos, while there will be “practical guidance” for councils on how to make towns more attractive.

Police will be able to shut “dodgy” barbers, vape shops and nail salons for twice as long - up to a year - to allow officers more time to investigate links to organised crime, under proposals first announced by Sir Keir Starmer’s government.

Mr Burnham said the changes would help put local communities “back in control” and bring town centres back to life.

He said: “For many people, the high streets they grew up with have been hollowed out and become unrecognisable over decades of decline.

“The rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for.

open image in gallery A vape shop in Soho. Vaping shops will also be regulated in a bid to help boost the British high street ( AFP/Getty )

“That’s not on. I said we would improve Britain’s high streets, and that’s exactly what we are starting to do.”

He added: “High streets are the beating heart of local communities, but for too long Westminster has stood by while they have been in decline. This government is committed to restoring our high streets and bringing back hope across Britain.”

The “aim to permit” policy was introduced when the Blair government, in which Mr Burnham was a minister, liberalised gambling laws in 2005.

The prime minister, who has returned from a holiday a little over a fortnight into the job, will spend much of August travelling the UK asking people how the government can improve their lives.

He will have a focus on reviving high streets and tackling the cost of living, while officials say he will be in “listening mode”.

The Centre for Social Justice think tank, which has found that Britain has lost nearly 1,800 pubs and bars while vape and tobacco shops have increased in number to almost 2,200 since 2016, welcomed the plans.

Joshua Nicholson, head of housing and communities at the think tank, said: “The government is right to give councils new powers to say no to these dodgy shops. High street renewal is vital to restoring security within our communities.”

But Sir James Cleverly, the shadow local government secretary, said: “Everyone can see what has happened to our high streets, with once-treasured shops being replaced by a smattering of rogue operators, many of which have links to organised crime and fraud.

“Labour’s business rates hikes have hollowed out our high streets, driving out the shops people want and leaving empty units for whoever is left standing to fill. Conservatives would cut business rates for high street firms and back the small businesses that give a town centre its character.

“Unless the government takes steps to support the high streets and hard-working businesses, Labour’s increases in planning regulation will just mean more empty and boarded up shops.”

News.title: WHO warns it is ‘chasing’ Ebola as death toll surpasses 1,900: ‘The virus is ahead of us’
News.content:

The most rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak ever recorded actually began in February, several months prior to its official declaration in mid-May, according to the World Health Organization, as responders in eastern Congo attempt to catch up.

Confirmed cases of Ebola during this outbreak have now reached 4,200, resulting in more than 1,900 deaths, according to recent government figures.

Speaking at a news conference, the WHO regional director for Africa Dr Mohamed Yakub Janabi explained that genetic sequencing revealed the earlier start.

He noted that initial cases were mistakenly diagnosed as other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid.

open image in gallery The outbreak declared on May 15 is unlike most previous ones for Ebola because the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for it has no approved vaccines or treatments ( Reuters )

"So we are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us," Janabi said.

Dr Thierno Balde, WHO's incident manager for the Ebola response, stated that the genetic sequencing was carried out under the leadership of Dr Steve Ahuka, head of the virology department at Congo’s National Institute for Biomedical Research.

The WHO assesses the worldwide risk of spread as low because Ebola is not airborne, making it far harder to transmit than respiratory viruses.

Cases identified outside the affected region have so far been promptly caught and contained without causing sustained transmission, the agency said.

The outbreak declared on May 15 is unlike most previous ones for Ebola because the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for it has no approved vaccines or treatments. Early testing was conducted for the more common type of Ebola, contributing to delays.

The outbreak is unfolding in some of the most challenging conditions imaginable, with strikes by some unpaid health workers, threats by rebel groups, anger from long-traumatized communities and misinformation asserting that Ebola isn’t real. Health teams travel remote, unpaved roads and have reported shortages of protective gear, while a vast population of displaced people struggles to find reliable water sources for washing hands.

This Ebola outbreak has killed more people at a quicker rate than any other, including the 2014-2016 outbreak in West Africa that is considered the worst on record with over 11,000 deaths out of at least 28,000 cases. That one took about eight months to reach 1,000 deaths.

open image in gallery Last week, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesu said Ebola is spreading faster than efforts to fight it ( AP )

Ebola is rare but highly contagious and can be contracted from bodily fluids such as vomit, blood or semen and with contaminated surfaces and materials such as bedding and clothing. The disease it causes is severe and often fatal.

Last week, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesu said Ebola is spreading faster than efforts to fight it. New cases are doubling in some hot spots, Tedros said on X after meeting with officials in the capital, Kinshasa.

Health authorities have said between 60% and 70% of new cases are recorded outside of contacts being monitored, and that the outbreak is spreading at an “alarming” rate.

Access to healthcare in the region already had been challenged by years of rebel conflict in one of Congo’s most remote and vulnerable areas, near the borders of South Sudan, Uganda and Rwanda. Now some pregnant women and others are avoiding health centers for fear of the virus, at risk to their lives.

Several past Ebola outbreaks have also been declared weeks or months late, including the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak. That outbreak was declared in March 2014, although the first human case later was found to have occurred in December 2013.

News.content:

Criminal fraud and bribery charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani were dismissed by a U.S. judge on Monday, following a decision by the Justice Department to drop the prosecution.

Brooklyn-based U.S. District Judge Nicholas Garaufis granted the rare request by federal prosecutors after questioning the reasoning behind the move, which included directly asking Adani if any promises were made in return for tossing out the case.

In November 2024, before the unsealing of the indictment, Adani committed to investing $10 billion in the United States.

The charges brought in 2024 alleged that Adani agreed to bribe Indian government officials so a subsidiary of the Adani Group could secure approval to build a solar energy plant.

Prosecutors contended that he subsequently misled U.S. investors by offering false assurances about the company's anti-corruption policies.

The Adani Group has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing. Adani has not appeared in a U.S. court to answer the charges.

The Justice Department announced on May 18 that it would no longer pursue the matter.

The decision represents the latest instance of federal prosecutors seeking to drop a high-profile white-collar prosecution during Republican President Donald Trump's second term in office.

Legal experts note that U.S. judges have little authority to force prosecutors to continue criminal cases they prefer to abandon, though charges cannot be formally dismissed without a judge's sign-off.

( Reuters )

Garaufis had asked the Justice Department to justify dropping the case, writing that its initial "bland and conclusory" announcement provided insufficient detail.

In a court filing on July 4, Trent McCotter, a senior Justice Department official, explained that the matter was primarily foreign, difficult to prove, and misaligned with the agency's current priorities.

McCotter also refuted media reports as false after they suggested he sought to throw out the case partly due to Adani's commitment to invest funds within the United States.

In response, Garaufis asked Adani directly whether he was "aware of any agreement exchanging anything for the dismissal of the indictment."

In a sworn declaration submitted on July 15, Adani stated that he was not aware of any such arrangement.

He recognized his prior pledge to invest $10 billion in the U.S. and noted his lawyers had told the Justice Department during meetings that the commitment "might be part of a resolution of these matters."

Robert Giuffra, an attorney representing Adani, stated in a court filing on July 15 that the Justice Department informed him it would not consider the Adani Group's willingness to invest in the U.S. as part of any resolution.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected

Jamie Vardy is a man without a club after leaving Cremonese and West Ham have him on their shortlist as they seek to add a new striker before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy could find himself back in England at the age of 39

West Ham are considering making a move for veteran frontman Jamie Vardy if they are unsuccessful with their pursuit of Troy Parrott.

‌



The former Leicester City forward wants to remain playing and is a free agent after his contract with Italian side Cremonese expired. It was his first spell playing outside of England and the Hammers could present the 39-year-old with the chance to return.

‌



Currently West Ham, who are gearing up for a first year in the Championship for more than a decade, have their sights on Parrott, formerly of Tottenham. The Irishman is now playing for AZ Alkmaar, where he has scored 51 goals in his two seasons.

‌



The Times reports that they've had a bid of £15million rejected and, if the Dutch side hold firm and refuse to sell their striker, then it could open the door for Vardy to make a move to the London Stadium. Another player on their shortlist was Wilson Isidor, but Sunderland have insisted he is not leaving.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Vardy spent the bulk of his career with the Foxes and was on their books when they won promotion from the Championship in 2014, he scored 16 times that year. Within two years he was a Premier League winner and proved himself to be a prolific marksman in the top flight.

Vardy scored 145 times in the top flight, putting him 14th on the all-time list, whilst he also won the Golden Boot in 2020. The former Fleetwood striker would win another Championship title with Leicester in 2022, scoring 20 times, and his experience could prove an asset for the Hammers as they seek an immediate return to the Premier League.

‌



The Hammers have just announced the signing of Manor Solomon, who penned a three-year deal after finalising a £7m switch from Tottenham. The winger was on loan at Leeds when they won promotion from the Championship in 2025.

View 2 Images West Ham are currently chasing Troy Parrott, but AZ Alkmaar have rejected their bids so far

West Ham are heavy favourites to win the Championship. They've managed to retain England international Jarrod Bowen whilst Nuno Espirito Santo has chosen to remain as manager. He won the second tier with Wolves back in 2017.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho admits his family have a better time when he's not around
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho admits his family have a better time when he's not around

Football manager Jose Mourinho rarely comments about his family life but says it remains important even if he seems football obsessed in new Netflix series.

View 2 Images Jose is back managing at Real and that mean there is unlikely to be much family time in the coming months. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho has admitted he doesn’t spend a lot of time with his family but insists his wife and kids enjoy life more when he is not there.

‌



The football manager has been married to his childhood sweetheart Matilde “Tami” Faria for more than 35 years, and they have two children – Matilde, 30, and Jose Mario Jr, 26.

‌



But the family seldom travelled with him around Europe as he managed Benfica, Porto, Chelsea, Manchester United, Roma, Inter Milan and Real Madrid over 25 years. He lived in the Lowry hotel in Manchester alone for much of his time there. For the majority of their upbringing the children lived in the West London family home while Jose travelled.

‌



In a new interview, Mourinho, 63, says: “Sometimes you have a feeling of, ‘I should be there, I’m not there.’ But I don’t want you to think that family means something less important to me. They are in a place that they cannot even be compared with football.

View 2 Images Mourinho in new Netflix doc (Image: Courtesy of Netflix)

“But to tell the truth, I know that they enjoy life much more without me. That’s real. It’s true. If they go to a restaurant with me, it’s different than going without me.”

‌



But Mourinho has continually stressed the importance of his marriage and family life. In 2014 he told the Mirror: “My wife trusts me, my wife knows me. She has been with me since I was 17 and she was 15 – everything is so crystal clear for us.

“My social life doesn’t exist. I have my professional work and I have my family life. I am not the kind of guy with a social life and I am so happy the way I am. The secret in everything is love. If you’re success- ful in any job, I believe it is because you are in love with that job.

“And if you have a successful family it is because people are in love with each other. Love is the basic.”

‌



Jose often credits Tami for his success as a manager. Speaking in a new Netflix documentary on his family as photos of them appear on screen, he says: “I try to protect as much as I can, but many times, of course, I fail. It’s not easy.

“The mum[Tami] is a great mum, and they understand that to be what I am in football, this is my way. They need to understand it. You are pushing me to speak about myself, which I don't want to.

“I think your happiness, your unhappiness, your problems, you leave it in the door of the training ground. Probably, it's an old-fashioned way of looking at things, but that's who I am, and in the end, I don't want to change. It's too late.”

‌



Mourinho is much more comfortable discussing his career and his coaching at clubs like Inter, Chelsea and Real where he had much success. He is now back at Real for a second stint as manager. In the documentary series he is shown joking that he is “peaceful” whilst on a walk by the coast where he is carrying two mobile phones to make calls and send messages to his team about matches and transfers.

Now back at Real, he also explains football is his life and says: “Football is a job that absorbs me. That's the way I am. No gardening, no cooking, no cleaning, no golf, no paddle, no nothing.”

Mourinho is also happy to play the villain in football and is not one to shy away from controversy. He says he does not regret criticising referee Anders Frisk who ended up getting death threats and quit football following a controversial Champions League game in 2005 between Chelsea and Barcelona.

‌



Mourinho said: “People say I spoke too much after that match, but I will do it again. That's the way. So I'm not nice. I'm not nice. Just the way it is.”

Ask how it feels to admit he is not nice, he adds: “I do it in a pride way, and you think to help your team to get results.”

* The three-part series Mourinho drops on Netflix today(August 11).

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish
Sports.content:
Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has been desperate for reinforcements in central defence following a difficult injury-hit pre-season - and now Ronald Araujo has arrived from Barcelona

View 3 Images Ronald Araujo has joined Liverpool on loan from Barcelona (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool have completed the signing of Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan deal - which could become a permanent switch if the Reds active the £47.14million option to buy.

‌



The 27-year-old Uruguay international moves from the Nou Camp in one of the more surprising switches of the summer so far. Last term he was still serving as the skipper for the Spanish giants, but has now opted for a move away after seeing his minutes decline.

‌



He is the second defender to arrive at Anfield this summer after Jeremy Jacquet completed his switch from Rennes, further bolstering a backline that already has Virgil van Dijk as its leader. Joe Gomez has been injured in pre-season and has struggled to remain consistently fit.

‌



Araujo has chosen the No 33 shirt - which was last worn a decade ago by Jordon Ibe. The centre-half becomes the fourth Uruguayan to play for the Reds - following in the footsteps of Darwin Nunez, Sebastian Coates and Luis Suarez.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club READ MORE :

Suarez remains one of the greatest Liverpool players of the Premier League era and was quick to reach out to his compatriot, congratulating him on his switch to Anfield.

‌



“We loved watching the English Premier League and everyone in Uruguay gets up early in the morning to catch the games," Araujo told the club's website.

“Of course as a kid I used to watch Luis playing all those fantastic games for Liverpool. We all know what he achieved, the history that he made within this club during his time here. So it’s fantastic.

“From minute one, I’ve been sort of asked about that kind of comparison since I’ve arrived here. I get on really well with him, we’re quite close. Just a few minutes ago I got a good luck message from him saying all the best, you’ve joined a great club and all the very best for your time here.”

‌



View 3 Images Luis Suarez reached out to Ronald Araujo (Image: Getty Images)

Araujo comes into a Liverpool side that have endured a difficult pre-season. On Sunday they squandered a two-goal lead for the second time in a matter of weeks, losing to Monaco in Andoni Iraola's first game at Anfield.

The Reds finished the friendly with youngster Luke Chambers and midfielder Wataru Endo as the centre-back pairing, underlining the need for new arrivals, with £55m signing Jacquet still getting fit.

‌



Iraola was critical post-match and admitted that the team were not capable of sustaining their level for the 90 minutes, raising questions over whether they can implement his philosophy.

"We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes," he said. "Right now we probably don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has been desperate for new signings (Image: Ian Horrocks, Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

‌



"We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game."

Iraola has made it clear that Liverpool need to make signings in the summer transfer window if they are to turn around their disappointing second campaign under Arne Slot. The Reds remain in the market for a world-class attacker, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola the number one target.

It has been a summer of upheaval for Liverpool, who changed manager before Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards decided to quit, piling more pressure onto sporting director Richard Hughes. Meanwhile, FSG have been busy negotiating a 30 per cent investment from a consortium which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Sports.title: 9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem
Sports.content:
It's been a summer of upheaval in the Premier League, with nearly half of the 20 sides opting to change manager in the off-season.

Clubs at both ends of the spectrum have put their faith in a new boss in the hope that the 2026/27 season will bring success. Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea have all changed tack, albeit for differing reasons, with Enzo Maresca chosen to succeed Pep Guardiola, while Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso have walked in after frustrating campaigns under previous coaches.

Fulham, Nottingham Forest, Ipswich, Crystal Palace, Newcastle and Bournemouth also have fresh - but in some cases familiar - faces in the dugout. They know just how high the stakes are, especially at Forest, who burnt through four managers last season.

It is extremely unlikely that all nine new bosses will see their plans come to fruition in the coming months, so who will sink and who will swim? Here Mirror Football attempts to rank them in terms of which has the best chance of achieving their goals.

‌



9. Fulham - Alvaro Arbeloa

Marco Silva left Fulham this summer for Benfica having achieved one of the most boringly successful, under-the-radar stints in Premier League managerial history. After bringing Fulham up as champions in 2021/22, he embarked upon (depending on your viewpoint) mid-table security or mid-table mediocrity: 10th, 13th, 11th, 11th. In short, he did a good job but without pulling up trees.

It is into this context that Arbeloa walks, the Real Madrid cast-off attempting to establish himself. I would suggest that signing two other Real Madrid cast-offs, in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, may not have been the best way to try and move on from your past.

Harry Wilson, Fulham's stand-out player from last season, and Raul Jimenez, their experienced striker, have both left. We have no evidence yet that Arbeloa has the tactical nous to craft a new playing style, or the force of personality to create a team bond. I fear they are going to struggle.

View 7 Images Alvaro Arbeloa may struggle at Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



8. Newcastle - Matthias Jaissle

You fear for Jaissle - and not because of anything he has done (yet). Newcastle have undergone a huge turnover this summer, selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, while also seeing Eddie Howe resign.

Howe was in situ for nearly five years and his exit was always going to cause instability. The fact his exit came alongside the departures of three key players means Newcastle are at risk of spiralling downwards after their 12th-place finish last season.

The Magpies' owners, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, have promised a lot and Jaissle is their man, having been recruited from the relative obscurity of Al-Ahli. Just 38 years old, the German has landed an exciting job, but an extremely difficult one.

Their new signings this summer fall into the camp of 'plenty of potential' rather than 'proven performers'. There is still some time to add some players from the latter section, but reports that Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has turned down the chance to join them suggests their transfer window woes could continue.

‌



View 7 Images Matthias Jaissle is the new man in charge at Newcastle (Image: 2026 Newcastle United)

7. Ipswich - Gary O'Neil

It's hard to judge O'Neil following a rollercoaster few years in management. But he won't have much time to settle in at Portman Road, having stepped into the breach following Kieran McKenna's surprise decision to walk away after leading the Tractor Boys to promotion.

O'Neil's star rose due to his spell at Bournemouth, fell after his time at Wolves - despite actually having a better win percentage - and then plateaued at Chelsea sister club Strasbourg. So is he one of the brightest English coaches in the game, or a middle-of-the-road one who has been over-promoted? We're about to get a better idea.

6. Liverpool - Andoni Iraola

View 7 Images Andoni Iraola has lots of problems to contend with (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola is obviously a brilliant coach and man-manager. His time at Bournemouth, in which he consistently improved the side, despite losing star after star to bigger clubs, earned him a shot at the big time. But pre-season has shown just how difficult the task is that he inherited from Arne Slot.

There are issues all over the pitch to address - from an ageing and injured central defence, through a central midfield which has lost its trademark high-energy pressing, to a misfiring (and extremely expensive) attack.

The job at Anfield is totally different to the one which the Spaniard became used to with the Cherries. He will have to manage egos, deal with heightened expectations, juggle the squad to cope with the Champions League, and - ultimately - win games straight away.

That will take time. This won't be a quick fix.

‌



5. Nottingham Forest - Oliver Glasner

Nuno Espirito Santo. Ange Postecoglou. Sean Dyche. Vitor Pereira. Forest went through all of them last season and still somehow managed to stay in the Premier League.

Glasner attracted plenty of interest when he announced he would leave Crystal Palace at the end of the season and eventually landed in Nottingham, where he will hope to buck the trend of notoriously impatient owner Evangelos Marinakis.

Glasner showed at Palace that he is an extremely shrewd operator with a clear playing style. He can drill players into his way of doing things. But, as we saw during his final months at Palace, he is not shy in voicing his frustrations when it comes to transfers. If he decides to take on Marinakis then it will only go one way.

View 7 Images Oliver Glasner has a completely different environment to deal with at Forest (Image: PA)

‌



4. Crystal Palace - Pierre Sage

The 47-year-old Frenchman arrived in south London after a seriously impressive one and only season with Lens, who he led to the Coupe de France final - the club's first since 1998 - and second place in Ligue 1.

The question is whether his success in France will translate into the Premier League with Palace following the successful reign of Glasner. Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira are proof that it doesn't always work out like Glasner when taking a manager from abroad.

Sage worked in academy football for years before ascending to first-team football. He is a calm head and will take a methodical approach with Palace, which should mean a steady succession.

3. Chelsea - Xabi Alonso

View 7 Images Xabi Alonso has a huge squad to whittle down at Chelsea (Image: Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Getty Images)

‌



Alonso knows how hard it could be for him. "I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," he said this summer. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them."

The Spaniard has been handed more control than his predecessors, which is shown by his "manager" title, rather than "head coach". He failed at Real Madrid, but was extremely impressive at Bayer Leverkusen and has a ludicrously stacked squad with which to create his own identity at Chelsea.

While some managers have found the Blues' embarrassment of riches a hindrance, preferring a smaller squad, Alonso could be the man to tame it. If he can strike the right balance, maintaining squad harmony while honing in on those players who suit his style, they could be onto a winner.

2. Bournemouth - Marco Rose

Bournemouth's reputation for being a well-run club is fully deserved. Their recruitment team continually strike gold when scouring the market for young, talented and under-valued players. That - plus Iraola's coaching - has allowed them to continue to thrive despite selling those players on a few years later.

‌



Rose has worked at Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, so has experience of 'bigger' clubs than Bournemouth. While he hasn't lasted long at either of the German giants, he has been hired due to his reputation as a coach who can get the best out of young players. Given their track record, I trust Bournemouth's judgement.

1. Manchester City - Enzo Maresca

View 7 Images Enzo Maresca has been groomed as Pep Guardiola's successor for some time

Pep Guardiola's successor has been groomed for many years for the role. Having worked under the City boss as a coach and soaked up his tactical philosophy, Maresca could hardly be more of a continuity pick.

The Italian left Chelsea under a cloud, but he has everything in place at City to succeed. Yes, following long-serving successful bosses is difficult, as David Moyes showed at Manchester United following Sir Alex Ferguson's departure. Maresca isn't walking into something unknown. He knows the club, he knows the players and he knows exactly what's expected of him in the City set-up. He's not Pep, but things aren't about to drop off a cliff.

‌

Sports.title: Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'
Sports.content:
Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'

Arsenal eyed up a blockbuster move for Vinicius Junior this summer but the Real Madrid star ultimately decided to stay put - and the Premier League side have since been mocked

View 2 Images Jon Obi Mikel has poked fun at Arsenal's standing as they looked to prise Vinicius Jnr from Real Madrid (Image: The Obi One Podcast)

Arsenal have been told they're not "one of the big boys" by John Obi Mikel, who has mocked them for believing they could ever sign Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Gunners were heavily linked with the Brazilian earlier this summer in what would've been a club-record move. Vinicius' contract was winding down and the Premier League champions were looking to seize on the uncertainty.

‌



It would've been a blockbuster transfer had Arsenal pulled it off, but the player ultimately decided to extend his stay at the Bernabeu, leaving the north Londoners to look elsewhere in a bid to bolster their forward line.

‌



But Mikel has laughed off the idea that Vinicius was ever going to move to Arsenal, insisting the club have got above their station after winning a first league title in two decades whilst still awaiting their first ever Champions League triumph.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

The former Chelsea midfielder said on The Obi One Podcast: "I don’t know what the Arsenal fans were expecting. You win the league after 22 years and then you all of a sudden think: that’s it, you’ve arrived, you’re one of the big boys again. No, you’re not.

"They’ve just been humbled because I said it: there’s no way Vinicius Junior is leaving Real Madrid to go to Arsenal, a club that’s won one title in 22 years. This guy wins titles, he’s won lots of titles at Real Madrid. He wants to win titles season after season, the Champions League, La Liga, competing year after year and winning those titles.

‌



"He’s tasted what it feels like winning the Champions League, Arsenal have never won the Champions League. Zero. You expect a player who has won the Champions League with Real Madrid to leave that."

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr has chosen to remain with Real Madrid (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Mikel believes that Real Madrid, who have Jose Mourinho at the helm once again, are assembling a team that can challenge for Europe's highest honour once again. They've already signed the likes of Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva and Yan Diomande.

Article continues below

Arsenal meanwhile have looked to build on their champion year and added Bruno Guimaraes at the weekend. The former Newcastle midfielder is their biggest capture of the summer so far, at £75m, and they're still in the market for a major frontline signing.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho fires clear dig at old foe Pep Guardiola: 'I hate that word'
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho fires clear dig at old foe Pep Guardiola: 'I hate that word'

Jose Mourinho hasn't spent a year out of management in more than two decades and has claimed he'll never take a sabbatical, suggesting its a sign of weakness

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho has underlined his desire to continue managing (Image: Netflix)

Jose Mourinho seems to have fired a dig at long-time rival Pep Guardiola as he claimed a "sabbatical means weakness" with the Catalan currently taking some time out.

‌



Guardiola has just ended his 10-year spell with Manchester City and, despite the offer of work in the international scene, he wants to take some time out. He famously took a year out after leaving Barcelona in 2012, before assuming his role at Bayern Munich.

‌



It was his years at Barcelona, where he faced Mourinho's Real Madrid, that prompted Guardiola's first sabbatical. The Catalan is ultimately renowned for his intensity and taking him away is only natural.

‌



However, the Special One has highlighted how he's never needed to spend time out of the game. His spells out of management have simply come whilst he's been waiting for a job to come up and Mourinho maintains sabbaticals aren't for him.

Jose Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd READ MORE :

He said in his Netflix Documentary: “Some guys, they need a sabbatical – which is something that I hate. I hate that word. For me, sabbatical means weakness. Don’t speak with me about sabbaticals. I never need a rest. I will have a rest when he (Mourinho points to the sky) decides to say: ‘Come up’.”

Since shooting to prominence with Porto in the early 2000s, the longest stint Mourinho has had out of management was 11 months - that coming between his Manchester United sacking in December 2018 and him taking on the Tottenham job in November 2019.

‌



Mourinho, now 63, has returned to Real this summer for a second spell and signed a three-year contract. The Portuguese boss admits he cannot foresee a day when he's not in management.

View 2 Images In contrast to Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho insists he wouldn't take a sabbatical (Image: PA)

He said: “I cannot even imagine when I am going to stop my life in football. I say 10 more years, but maybe more than 10. It’s fun. It was, it is and will always be fun. I want to win more titles. I want to win new titles. I want to repeat titles.

‌



“I want to do it in places where I have never been. I want to do it in places where I did before. My world is to walk in a football stadium with 50,000 or 90,000 [fans]. I had 100,000. That is my world.

“Without football, there is not something complete in me. But I don’t think it is an obsession. I don’t feel it as an obsession. It is just when you reach a certain level, you want to stay there forever.”

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Araujo from Barcelona
Sports.content:
Liverpool have confirmed the signing of defender Ronald Araujo from Barcelona.

The deal is an initial loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract with Barca until 2031 last year, and also includes an option to buy for around £47.14m (€55m).

⁠Liverpool are not paying Barcelona a loan fee and will cover the entirety of Araujo's salary for the duration of the season-long loan. It is understood Araujo has taken a pay cut to facilitate the move.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool sign Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on loan with an option to buy.

Araujo, who will wear the No 33 shirt, told Liverpoolfc.com: "I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy.

"I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my team-mates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

"I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

"As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time."

The Uruguay international, who did not play at the World Cup due to injury, is expected to train with his new team-mates this week.

Araujo will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

Jacquet, a summer signing from Rennes, has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre-back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully-fit senior centre-back.

Image: Liverpool have signed Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan

Araujo, who can play at right-back and centre-back, moved from his native Uruguay in 2018 and made his Barcelona debut the following October, going on to play more than 200 games for the LaLiga side.

He was named as one of the club captains following the departure of Marc-Andre ter Stegen in January, but started only 11 LaLiga matches for the Catalan giants last season after an extended break from football in November 2025 to recover from what he later revealed was depression.

Why the Araujo deal works for Liverpool...

Liverpool had not been actively seeking out defensive reinforcements, their priority firmly on adding a wide forward, but this was a market opportunity that made sense for a number of reasons.

Ronald Araujo can play at centre-back or right-back, and, crucially, he was available on loan. This offered an appropriate solution to injury concerns that are deemed to be more short-term.

Liverpool have already committed £60m to signing Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes, with a view to him partnering Virgil van Dijk at centre-back.

However, it remains to be seen if he will be fit for the start of the season, as Liverpool take caution with his re-integration to competitive action following a shoulder injury that has kept him out since February.

A muscle problem for Joe Gomez, which will keep him out for the Premier League opener against Newcastle, has worsened the problem for new head coach Andoni Iraola, who by his own admission is slim on options at the back.

Araujo arriving on a temporary move alleviates that injury headache and adds a layer of experience to Liverpool's backline that is sorely missing. He has played more than 200 games for Barcelona after all.

There are understandable concerns around whether Araujo can turn around his struggles with form and fitness. Liverpool are not short on defenders with patchy injury records.

Liverpool are taking on a deal with an element of risk in that regard. But there is also a potentially big reward if Araujo does rediscover his best form thanks to the option to buy inserted in the deal worth around £47m.

At the peak of his powers, Araujo was being valued at around double that figure. Liverpool will hope to see his best in the Premier League, a division which is seemingly suited to his strengths.

How Liverpool were able to get Araujo

This is a deal that suits all parties. Liverpool require defensive cover amid injury worries around a number of players, while Araujo is not part of Hansi Flick's plans at Barcelona and is in need of a fresh start.

Araujo signed a new contract with Barcelona last year in January that reportedly put him among the club's highest earners. Six months earlier, he had been named Barcelona's vice-captain.

However, the Uruguay defender has since been unable to reach the heights that earned him such high status at Barcelona amid struggles with injury and his mental health.

Araujo wore the captain's armband as Barcelona celebrated becoming champions of Spain in May, but he had only played 24 times throughout the season.

Flick admitted when confirming the deal that Araujo was not suited to the way he wants to play and said the defender was excited about having the chance to move to a new environment.

Barcelona can now bring in a defender that Flick wants to work with, and Araujo has the opportunity to rebuild his career in the Premier League. If he performs, they will either earn a decent fee from Liverpool or his value will increase.

Sports.title: Sciver-Brunt helps Trent Rockets Women into Hundred final
Sports.content:
England all-rounder Nat Sciver-Brunt timed her introduction to perfection as 32 off 19 balls batting down the order secured Trent Rockets' progress to the final of The Hundred with a seventh successive victory.

Chasing 118 to win, the league leaders slipped to 10-3 against Southern Brave, the lowest powerplay score in the history of the competition, and even though passing 27 guaranteed their place in the final, the result remained in doubt.

Sciver-Brunt came in at number seven with the score on 66-5 and with 31 deliveries remaining - Ash Gardner having top-scored with 37 - and her experience avoided further drama.

She was run out going for a second which would have clinched victory, but Rockets still won with two balls to spare.

Southern Brave's 117-5 was built around their top order with Maia Bouchier scoring 38, Lizelle Lee 31 and Laura Woolvaardt adding 24.

They will get a second chance as they had already secured a place in the eliminator on Friday at The Kia Oval. Brave will discover their opponents on Tuesday, who will either be third-placed SunRisers Leeds or fourth-placed Manchester Super Giants who play each other at Emirates Old Trafford in their final group match.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Georgia Adams was run out in unfortunate fashion after Sarah Glenn fumbled a drive from Nat Sciver-Brunt and deflected the ball on to the stumps

Sciver-Brunt said: "I'm happy to be on the winning side. The wicket was a bit slow, and they bowled pretty well in the first half."

On batting down the order, she said: "It was a bit tactical and a bit injury management. We have got a lot of people in form and high on confidence. We have balanced our side nicely and building up to Sunday we sort of know what we need to do."
