Sports.title: Rangers meeting Q&A: McInnes-Klopp compared, club failure admission & new signings update
Sports.content:
Rangers chairman Andrew Cavanagh believes the Ibrox side have become used to finishing second or worse over the last 15 years, and admits that failure had begun to "seep through" every corner of the club.

He was speaking at the club's shareholders' meeting, where it was also revealed they expect to add three to five more players this window, while Derek McInnes' appointment was compared to that of former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

It was also confirmed that Rangers have asked for an explanation over Hibernian's penalty in Sunday's 2-1 defeat as refereeing concerns were raised.

Image: Jim Gillespie was appointed Rangers chief executive in January

Chairman Andrew Cavenagh, Paraag Marathe of the San Francisco 49ers [who are part of the US consortium who took over the club], executive director Fraser Thornton and chief executive officer Jim Gillespie addressed a number of club issues and answered questions from the floor.

Here are some of the key takeaways...

On Derek McInnes

Image: Derek McInnes left Hearts to take charge of Rangers this summer

During the meeting, one shareholder asked why Derek McInnes, the man they wanted to ask questions to after a winless start to the season, was absent. Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago and that McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team.

When asked later about the process behind hiring McInnes, Jim Gillespie said you can either hire a 'Klopp' or a 'Guardiola' type. He said McInnes fitted the 'Klopp' type of being a manager who wants his teams to be agressive, on the front foot and attack the opposition.

During the summer when McInnes was appointed, Sky Sports News revealed he was the only candidate who was spoken to, and Gillespie defended that by adding he was the only option Ibrox chiefs felt "ticked all the boxes".

Cavenagh reminded shareholders that "culture eats strategy for breakfast", and when speaking about standards, revealed people had been late to training and not eating well. He went on to say he believed McInnes was the right man to address this.

On Recruitment

Image: Daisuke Yokota is one of nine summer signings at Rangers so far

Multiple shareholders raised concerns about player recruitment. However, Cavenagh defended the work in that department, adding he believes the squad is better than it was 12 months ago.

He admitted the team still requires between three and five more players before the end of the transfer window.

The meeting was called following a £16m share issue. Cavenagh confirmed that was needed to get the club through this "significant" summer transfer window. He added the club "will need more capital going forward".

Marathe insisted that they were "building something special" and referenced Youssef Chermiti's performances in the second half of last season, after initially struggling with the pressure of his price tag and playing for Rangers.

Image: Youssef Chermiti was injured in Sunday's defeat to Hibs, hours after it was revealed a bid had been rejected for the striker

On Chermiti, the club hierarchy were asked why he was selected for Sunday's match against Hibernian despite being the subject of a bid from Galatasaray. The striker was subsequently stretched off injured in the first half of that defeat.

It was explained that to accept a bid, Rangers need their value of the player to be met, and for sufficient time to reinvest those funds in the squad to make it equal or better. They reiterated there is no pressure to sell.

On Refereeing standards

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian were awarded a first-half penalty in their 2-1 win at Rangers

Gillespie said that Rangers should be a leading club and want to have a constructive relationship with the Scottish FA and SPFL, while also holding both to account.

He was interrupted by a shareholder who said: "It's not working. It's been going on for years, nothing happens."

Marathe replied: "You're not wrong" but backed up Gillespie by saying, "we can't make it worse, we can't be in any more of what feels like a disadvantage".

Marathe added "he couldn't believe" the decision to award Hibernian a penalty in the first half of Sunday's match at Ibrox. Gillespie confirmed that Rangers have made contact with the Scottish FA to seek an explanation.

On Ibrox stadium

Image: Ibrox could be redeveloped with several proposals being considered

Marathe - who has overseen stadium expansion at Leeds United and the 49ers - discussed possible changes at Ibrox.

He said there would be news on that soon, while revealing one proposal is to lower the pitch at Ibrox, adding 5,000 to 6,000 seats.

It was also revealed, following fan surveys, a number of other ideas have been through a feasibility group and seen by architects.

Call for unity

Sports.title: Chelsea get Luton as Spurs to host Charlton in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Chelsea will host Jack Wilshere's Luton Town in the Carabao Cup second round, while Tottenham Hotspur host Charlton Athletic in a London derby.

Former Arsenal midfielder Wilshere will take his League One outfit to Stamford Bridge, as the 11 Premier League sides not involved in European competition this season joined the winners of the first-round ties in the hat.

Among the other tasty ties are League One AFC Wimbledon visiting Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham at Craven Cottage, while Keith Andrews' Brentford face a potentially tricky tie against Birmingham at St Andrew's.

Sports.title: Man City in Bouaddi talks and Chelsea's Fernandez also an option
Sports.content:
Man City are in ongoing talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Personal terms have been in place for a while with the 18-year-old as the clubs work to find an agreement.

As things stand, City do not consider talks with Barcelona for Rodri to be active after what they felt was a derisory opening offer, understood to be worth in the region of £40m.

The Spain captain is due to report back at City on Friday following his post-World Cup break. He has one year left on his deal and City would like him to renew.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Rodri linked with a move away from Manchester City, Sky Sports News reporter Ben Ransom discusses whether Ayyoub Bouaddi could be brought in to replace the midfielder

Sky Sports News understands Barcelona are considering their next offer for the 30-year-old.

Alongside Bouaddi, City are interested in several other midfielders, who could be turned to in the event of further sales. Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez is a player that they have on their list this summer.

Chelsea value the Argentina midfielder at £120m. He shared a strong working relationship with new City boss Enzo Maresca at Chelsea.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso discusses why Reece James will stay club captain under him and reveals he is looking forward to working with Enzo Fernandez

Who could leave Manchester City?

In terms of outgoings, City are aware of interest from Nottingham Forest in midfielder Tijjani Reijnders, who was signed from AC Milan last summer for £46m.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to stay and see out the final year of his deal at the Etihad.

Midfielder Nico Gonzalez has said he wants to stay, but it remains to be seen if his opportunities will improve under Maresca.

The City boss has said Omar Marmoush will decide his future at City, likening his situation to James Trafford's who has subsequently joined Leeds United.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the friendly between Manchester City and Atletico Madrid

Marmoush wants to play more minutes, and Maresca has left the door open for that to happen under him at City this season.

At this stage, there has been no fresh contact for Tottenham target Savinho, who wants to leave City to join Spurs.

Meanwhile, Vitor Reis is expected to stay with Man City this season and fight for a first-team place.

The 20-year-old Brazilian has impressed new manager Enzo Maresca on the Far East tour, after spending last season on loan at sister club Girona. He joined City 18 months ago for just under £30m.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and England players Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson are due back at City on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Scotland, Netherlands criticise Cricket World Cup format changes
Sports.content:
Scotland and the Netherlands have criticised the restructuring of next year's 50-over World Cup, saying the changes "risk weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket".

At last month's board meeting in Edinburgh, the International Cricket Council announced the main part of the tournament in southern Africa will contain a dozen teams split into two groups of six.

There will still be 14 participants, but the tournament is slated to start with a preliminary round involving the three lowest-ranked qualifiers, with only one team progressing to the group stage.

A qualifying tournament will be held from February 22 to March 23 next year, with the winner going through to the main tournament and the second, third and fourth placed teams entering the first round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia are reigning 50-over champions having defeated India in the 2023 World Cup final

In a joint statement, Cricket Scotland and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association (KNCB) said they were "deeply disappointed" by the ICC's decision, announced less than 18 months before the tournament is due to start.

The statement said: "At a time when cricket is seeking to expand its reach, attract new audiences and strengthen its position on the international sporting landscape, reducing meaningful opportunities for emerging nations sends entirely the wrong message.

New Cricket World Cup format Round One: Teams 12, 13, 14 in round-robin ‘Super Series’

Teams 12, 13, 14 in round-robin ‘Super Series’ Top team progresses to Round Two

Round Two: Two groups of six teams (30 matches)

Two groups of six teams (30 matches) Top three teams in each group plus next best across both qualify

Round 3: Super 7 – Round robin (21 matches)

Super 7 – Round robin (21 matches) Top four teams progress to semi-finals

Semi-finals

Final

"We have significant concerns about both the impact of these changes and the process through which they have been introduced.

"The changes risk weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket, and only highlight the importance of strong governance, transparent decision-making and effective engagement with members."

Scotland and the Netherlands are currently 13th and 14th respectively in the men's ODI rankings.

Sports.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
Sports.content:
Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”.

In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

The three confederations have started preliminary discussions about the organisation of new competitions along with Uefa’s repeated threats to boycott Fifa events. As things stand, the under-20 women’s World Cup next month could take place without European teams and alternative options are being sought.

The letter is signed by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, his AFC counterpart, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, and the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani. Efforts to unite around a suitable candidate to replace Infantino have stepped up since his privately backed plan was revealed and Montagliani is believed to be among the contenders.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter reads. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It strongly criticises Fifa’s response to the crisis, when a meeting between a small number of senior staff in Rabat was followed by an apology from Infantino that appeared not to show remorse for the scheme.

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment,” the letter says. “It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment – not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. He is believed to be interested in running for the Fifa presidency. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

The three presidents also call for an independent review, conducted by a body outside football, into the affair. Fifa had committed previously to presenting a full report to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting.

The letter directly addresses concerns that countries may lose out on financial aid under a different leadership, saying it is “[not] about any member association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our leadership to suggest otherwise”.

The letter concludes: “There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness … Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, with leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

51:14 Infantino hangs on by a thread and the overhaul at Newcastle | Football Weekly – video

Any candidates for the Fifa election must announce their bid by 18 November. The confederations are understood to consider all options in their push for Infantino to be replaced, provided they fit within Fifa’s statutes and governance framework.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

While the letter outlines the stances of the three confederations, and particularly their leaderships, the story is more complicated within individual member associations. Few outside Europe have been willing to come out publicly against Infantino and only a small minority have been tempted to recall the letters of support they had sent backing his re‑election next March. The influential African and South American confederations, Caf and Conmebol, have come out backing Infantino in recent days.

A number of larger member associations have written to Infantino asking for a meeting where he would be required to explain his actions around the FFE scheme. No response has been received. Nor has Infantino been in touch with federations to address his leading role in the turmoil.

The confederations’ tripartite statement was followed by another joint release headed by the World Cup hosts US Soccer and Canada Soccer, who along with the Caribbean Football Union and Central American Football Union also called for governance change at Fifa.

The four bodies comprise 40 of the 41 Concacaf members, with the outliers being the third World Cup hosts Mexico, who went public last Friday with their continued support for Infantino.

US Soccer had previously been silent and its willingness to condemn Fifa is significant, particularly as it is bidding to host the 2031 Women’s World Cup and also wants to stage games at the 2029 Club World Cup.

“US Soccer, Canada Soccer, CFU [Caribbean Football Union] and UNCAF [Central American Football Union] stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens Fifa’s governance, transparency and accountability,” the statement read.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 2: Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

The image of John McGinn hoisting aloft the Europa League trophy in Istanbul as the confetti cannons fired is crystallised in the minds of Aston Villa supporters, but less than three months on, plenty has changed since one of the club’s greatest days. Three major players from the starting lineup – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, two of whom scored – have exited, and another may follow if Arsenal make a serious play for the dependable Ezri Konsa.

A key trio of coaches have also left – the set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, assistant manager Pako Ayestarán and the influential individual coach, Antonio Rodríguez Saravia – but most importantly the common denominator and driver of Villa’s incredible rebirth remains in post. It is a good job Unai Emery enjoys a challenge. It has been a typically busy summer, with pre-season trips to Portugal, Indonesia and Hong Kong, plus the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday and a friendly trip to Mönchengladbach to follow, but there is work to do if Emery is to repeat the feat of fourth place and break new ground, again, by securing Champions League qualification for successive campaigns.

After a terrible start, Villa edged over the line last season, but the landscape is unlikely to be so forgiving this time. Nobody played more minutes for Villa than Rogers and it was no surprise Villa’s alarming drop in form around spring coincided with Tielemans being injured. Villa need their replacements to work. João Gomes, a £38m buy from Wolves, looks a smart fit; the tigerish Brazil midfielder made the third-highest number of tackles in the division last season (107) and was fourth on the list for ball recoveries (194). Johan Manzambi is one of the game’s most exciting young talents, while Emery believes he can rehabilitate Alejandro Garnacho, who has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea.

Only Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester City have amassed more Premier League points in the three-and-a-half years since Emery arrived, and while it would be foolish to write him off, every season his task seems to get that bit harder. He can still call on a core cast of reliable performers in Konsa, McGinn, Matty Cash, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins, while Boubacar Kamara’s return from injury this month is a timely boost. But it is hard not to wonder whether Villa have peaked.

Off-field picture

The response of a senior executive was telling when asked if qualifying for the Champions League makes life easier when it comes to meeting the financial rules. “Not easier but less difficult,” came the reply. Villa have since signed a lucrative shirt sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, worth about £20m per season, though Amnesty International warns Rwanda “is using sportswashing to deflect attention from its terrible human rights record”. Meanwhile, Villa Park’s makeover continues with the North Stand closed for the season, the stadium’s capacity falling to 37,000 during its redevelopment. The new-look stand will have a steel roof, modern facade and accommodate more than 12,000 fans - bringing the overall capacity past 50,000 supporters - and will be ready for 2027-28 and Euro 2028.

Owner-fan relationship

Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens will always be adored for putting Villa firmly back on the map, elevating them to become major Premier League players and, ultimately, as the people who gave Emery the keys to transform the club. Both joined the on-field celebrations in Istanbul in May, Sawiris with a claret-and-blue scarf around his neck. Michael Angelakis, chair of investment company Atairos and chief executive of Comcast, acquired a minority stake in 2023. The story goes that Sawiris, Egypt’s richest man, handed Emery a blank sheet of paper and asked him to design his vision when meeting the Basque for the first time in Madrid, at the home of the agent Jorge Mendes.

The manager

“He lives like a monk in a tracksuit,” was how Villa’s director of football operations and Emery’s right-hand man, Damian Vidagany, described the 54-year-old manager’s work ethic in the book Waking The Giant. During the season it is not unusual for Emery, who has an apartment in Birmingham city centre, to spend 12 hours a day at Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, sometimes analysing footage on his laptop while on the exercise bike or treadmill, long after his players have gone. Emery’s squad have grown accustomed to long meetings, sometimes twice a day – one was held less than 12 hours after cementing their place in the Champions League after beating Liverpool in May, in preparation for Emery to clinch a record fifth Europa League title of his coaching career.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi looks pleased to be wearing the claret and blue. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

There were a few nerves at Villa as Manzambi illuminated Switzerland’s World Cup, concerns his price could balloon or that bigger fish may blow them out of the water. But Villa had done their homework and got a longstanding target over the line for a club-record £51m amid interest from rivals. Manzambi was on Villa’s radar long before he impressed against them for Freiburg in the Europa League final. Murat Yakin, the Switzerland head coach, described Manzambi as “a street footballer”, saying the 20-year-old’s humility and quality means he is capable of playing across the pitch. He played regularly as a No 8 in the Bundesliga and Emery is an admirer of his versatility.

Stat attack

Aston Villa scored 15 goals from outside the box last season. Seven teams had recorded more in one of the previous 17 Premier League campaigns, but no side in that period bettered their 8.4% shot conversion rate. As only 3.6% of attempts from this range are converted on average, Villa’s 2025-26 tally feels impossible to repeat.

Set for a breakthrough

It will be interesting to see if the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, son of former Plymouth and Shrewsbury forward Guy, can build on his encouraging pre-season form. Emery and his coaches are big fans of Madjo, a physical striker born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, so no wonder this month Villa welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) clearing Madjo to feature after Fifa rules prohibited him from playing after joining from Metz in a £10m deal in January. “English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo,” McGinn posted on social media. It has been a whirlwind 12 months for Madjo: he made his Ligue 1 debut last August aged 16, before scoring on debut for England Under-17s a few weeks later. Four goals in pre-season has led to a sense that his first competitive minutes for Villa are close.

World Cup impact

Amadou Onana, whose Villa career has been stop-start owing to injury, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in Belgium’s last-16 win over the USA. Manzambi enjoyed a fine World Cup, even if his tournament also ended with a knee injury, ruling him out of Switzerland’s last 16 and quarter-final matches and delaying his Villa debut. Martínez made it to another final with Argentina. Konsa started every game for England before the semi-final against Argentina: his 72nd-minute introduction from the bench for Anthony Gordon widely pinpointed as a negative change that invited pressure.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over fan banner
Sports.content:
The Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Crystal Palace for defamation after supporters of the south London club displayed a banner depicting him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Almost 12 months since the banner appeared midway through the first half of Palace’s 1-1 draw with Forest at Selhurst Park, lawyers for Marinakis lodged the claim for defamation against CPFC Ltd and “persons unknown” at the high court on Monday.

The banner showed the Greek shipping magnate pointing the gun at Gibbs-White, who had been set to join Tottenham last summer before Forest pulled out of the deal, and also featured the message: “Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match‑fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.” Marinakis has previously rejected all those allegations. Lawyers for Marinakis were approached for comment. A spokesperson for Palace did not comment.

Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association in February after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

Last summer, Palace and Forest were at loggerheads after Forest wrote to Uefa to voice their concerns that Palace could be in breach of multiclub ownership rules. The FA Cup winners ended up being demoted to the Conference League, with Forest – who had finished seventh in the Premier League and originally qualified for the Conference League – promoted in their place. Palace went on to win that competition under Oliver Glasner, while Forest reached the Europa League semi-finals.

Glasner has since joined Forest after leaving Palace at the end of his contract in a move that has surprised both sets of supporters. The Austrian said this week that Marinakis had persuaded him to change his mind over dinner in Athens after previously rejecting Forest because they were not in Europe next season.

“Then I had a more detailed look and there are two reasons why I changed my mind and I told him,” Glasner said. “No 1 is I think there is more potential in the squad than they have shown. And No 2 is you, it’s your ambition, because I am very ambitious.”

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Self-aggrandisement, backslapping and news from the past: it’s José time
Sports.content:
TUDUM …

“You don’t do a documentary with a guy who wins nothing,” parps José Mourinho during the trailer for his shiny, new Netflix film, although since 2017, his sole piece of silverware is the 2021-22 Tin Pot with Roma. And while his failure to win anything with Tottenham, Fenerbahce or Benfica didn’t exactly – on paper, at least – make him the most obvious candidate as the author of that opening quote, neither does he immediately feel like the best man to put Florentino Pérez’s Death Star back on course in Madrid.

And yet, here we are. Just like the cagey 1-0 wins at Chelsea after which Mourinho would come out and explain that his team played like Brazil ‘82, the Portuguese has willed the narrative into existence: Mourinho is, apparently, one of the best managers on the planet and his documentary, in which lots of retired talking heads will wax lyrical about his achievements 20 years ago, finds its way to your screens on Tuesday. And it will be lapped up. Partly because of the warm glow of nostalgia, partly because pretty much everyone in the northern hemisphere can’t bear to be outside in this heat, and partly because, for a good few years, Mourinho really was the best thing since Steffi Graf’s sliced backhand: at Porto, at Chelsea, at Inter and yes, even sometimes at Madrid.

Amid all the pomp, the self-aggrandisement and the backslapping, the documentary does include a few nice little nuggets from the past, namely Mourinho’s claim that he was in line to replace Alex Ferguson as manager of Manchester United in 2013, before tearfully pulling out at the last minute. “I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” he teases. “When I left Real Madrid [the first time], I signed with Manchester United to go to United after Sir Alex.” Ferguson, also part of the doc, adds: “He phoned me and he was crying. And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

While some cynics would argue that simultaenously signing a contract with United and giving Chelsea his word before spontaneously bursting into tears is exactly the sort of illicit chaos that Mourinho became famous for, few would argue that he remains absolutely box office, win, lose or draw. Roll on Real Madrid, then, famously a serene meadow of footballing tranquillity where ego, pressure and scrutiny do not dare to darken the door. Netflix would be wise to get the cameras back in; this season would make one heck of a documentary.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club. Nobody knows that more than me … Every Rangers team is a byproduct of that frustration. The Rangers fans just want to see their team winning and so do I. And we will get there. I’m not going to ask the fans for more patience because I think the Rangers fans have been patient enough” – Derek McInnes there, now very much under the pump after his team slumped five points behind Celtic in the Scottish Premiership after just two games, losing 2-1 to Hibs at Ibrox.

View image in fullscreen Early-season dejection scenes at Ibrox. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Even allowing for my team, Hearts’, disjointed recent hire and exits, I do think we have had incredibly bad luck in all our European draws. First it was Sturm Graz, now Benfica, and next, in Tin Pot, it seems likely we’ll get Rapid Vienna. I’ve actually heard of every one of these teams. Why couldn’t we have got some other made-up team from an even worse league than the Scottish Premiership? Or is getting out of Europe before the end of August the only thing that might help us in the league?” – Ken Muir.

It really did remind me of the old Luigi Ferraris, where I spent nearly every Sunday in the early 80s. My mate was supporting the cyclists (Sampdoria) and me, of course, Genoa … we were taking each other to the home matches. I only went once to the one rebuilt for Italia 90 and found it so ugly and soulless. Some background in one of the local TV archives” – Giuseppe.

Sports.title: Jordan Nobbs ready to complete wishlist with Newcastle WSL dream
Sports.content:
Jordan Nobbs says winning promotion to the Women’s Super League with Newcastle would fulfil her ambition for a north‑east club to be in the top tier.

Nobbs, who has 71 England caps, was born in Stockton‑on‑Tees and believes women’s football in the region would benefit immensely from top‑flight representation. Newcastle finished sixth in WSL2 last season, 11 points behind the title winners, Birmingham, and nine points off the playoffs, but this summer they have made their hopes clear with high-calibre signings from the top division, including the striker Martha Thomas from Tottenham and the Liverpool duo Leanne Kiernan and Gemma Evans.

Nobbs is clear about the target for the new campaign. “It is promotion. I know we said it last season [too],” she said. “I’ve always said things don’t happen overnight, [but] that is our goal. You have to say it out loud.

“Looking back on last season, we had some really good performances but nine draws, that’s too many points [dropped]. It’s just about focusing on finding a way to win. We’ve just got to build on the good stuff from last season, I don’t think we’re far off it.

“[Winning promotion with Newcastle], I’ve always said it would be job done. I think to get a northern team promoted … as I heard from Newcastle I was like, that is exactly what I want to do. In the WSL, I’d ticked as much as I possibly could, so to get a north‑east team, which we all had to leave back in the day, promoted would be an achievement I would love.”

Nobbs began her career with Sunderland and broke into their team in the old top flight, but moved to Arsenal when the WSL was launched in 2011 and Sunderland’s application to join the breakaway division was rejected. That led to a successful team also including Nobbs’s future England teammates Lucy Bronze and Lucy Staniforth breaking up.

Sunderland did compete in the top tier between 2015 and 2018, but north-east representation in the WSL has been sparse, so Nobbs is pleased to see investment in recent years at Newcastle as well as their WSL2 rivals, who were taken over in June by Bay Collective.

“It’s been a long time coming, but it was something us northerners have always wanted,” Nobbs said. “We don’t want the north-east to fizzle out. We want to show the players that have come from there and developed there.

“It’s definitely grown in the right direction now, which is what we wanted. But the big stepping stone would be getting into the WSL. That would be where we really put the north-east back on the map and I’d love to be a part of that.”

The 33-year-old has enjoyed her role in Tanya Oxtoby’s setup at Newcastle after joining them last July. “With Villa I played a lot of a deeper role and [now] I really love being back in my high position, scoring goals, assisting and [I’m] in my happy place. I feel like I found that little spark again [last season] that was nice.”

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt stormed to European Championships gold with a blistering effort in the 100m, finishing in 11 seconds flat - having been in fifth at the 50m mark.

It's the latest statement of intent in a burgeoning career that could see the Grantham-born sprinter reach the pinnacle of her sport.

Prior to her triumph on Monday night, Daily Mail Sport sat down with the 'sexy and aggressive' athlete on her remarkable rise.

Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Aston Villa dealt blow in loan pursuit of Real Madrid star Endrick - with Jose Mourinho making a decision on Brazilian forward's future
Sports.content:
Aston Villa dealt blow in loan pursuit of Real Madrid star Endrick - with Jose Mourinho making a decision on Brazilian forward's future

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa's hopes of taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid have been dashed by the LaLiga club's decision to keep him.

The Brazilian forward's future had been in limbo, with the youngster waiting to see if he is part of Jose Mourinho's plans for this season as he wants to establish himself in Madrid.

Had Mourinho not included Endrick in his plans, he may have been forced to seek a temporary move away as he did last season with Lyon.

But Daily Mail Sport understands that the legendary former Chelsea boss wants to include Endrick in his first team plans moving forwards, dealing a hammer blow to any pursuit from Villa.

The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024 after he turned 18, with a deal having been agreed two years before.

He has scored seven goals in 40 appearances for Los Blancos but joined Lyon for the second half of 2025-26 after struggling for regular gametime.

Endrick impressed in France, netting five goals and adding seven assists in 16 appearances.

Aston Villa are among the list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid

Real boss Jose Mourinho is set to make a decision on the Brazilian forward in the near future

That form was enough for him to earn a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, yet despite significant clamour back home, the 20-year-old only played 111 minutes at the tournament.

Endrick failed to score during that time as Carlo Ancelotti's side suffered an embarrassing exit in the last-16 stage at the hands of Norway.

Villa are looking for attacking reinforcements following the departures of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans this summer, while there is uncertainty over the future of backup striker Tammy Abraham.

Ollie Watkins was also linked with Fenerbahce last month and Unai Emery's side sold Lucas Digne to PSG over the weekend.

They have so far added Switzerland World Cup breakout star Johan Manzambi and Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes.

Emery's side kick off their season with the UEFA Super Cup against PSG on Wednesday night, before they travel to Brighton next weekend in the Premier League.

Sports.title: City still want Bouaddi, West Ham interested in signing free agent Jamie Vardy as striker prepares to return to England - and Newcastle talks with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg break down: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City not giving up on Bouaddi

Manchester City are continuing discussions with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is keen to join City now rather than wait another season, which was Lille's preference, and the clubs are working towards agreement on a fee.

City still want another midfielder for when Rodri joins Barcelona with talks ongoing over a fee for the Spain captain.

Tottenham are continuing to monitor developments with Omar Marmoush and Savinho while Nottingham Forest want Tijjani Reijnders.

City and Southampton have agreed a season-long loan deal for Divin Mubama, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport. The 21-year-old forward spent last season on loan at Stoke City making 28 appearances in all competitions prior to damaging ankle ligaments in January.

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen to join Man City this summer

Wrexham want Leeds forward Gelhardt

Leeds forward Joe Gelhardt is wanted by Wrexham in a £4.5million deal.

The 24-year-old has spent the past two seasons on loan at Hull City and played a key part in their Championship promotion campaign last season scoring 14 league goals.

Wrexham recognise he could play a similar role for them as they attempt to take the next big step up into the top flight.

Hull have also considered a return for Gelhardt but are working on other targets including Swansea City's Zan Vipotnik.

Chelsea line up LA Galaxy youngster

Chelsea are close to finalising a deal for 16-year-old LA Galaxy midfielder Vicente Garcia.

The deal is expected to be worth £2.25m plus add-ons and Garcia would join Chelsea when he turns 18 in 2028.

Hojbjerg talks with Toon break down

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, became a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Full story

The Denmark star is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested

Newcastle winger Murphy set for Kaiserslautern

Newcastle United defender Alex Murphy is on the verge of a season-long loan move to Kaiserslautern.

The Republic of Ireland U21 international, who can play centre-back and left-back, is having a medical ahead of joining the Bundesliga 2 club.

Liverpool's Morrison wanted by Groningen

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is attracting interest from FC Groningen among other clubs. The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international will be allowed to leave on loan.

Morrison, who started out at Manchester United, made his international debut in June against Guinea.

Tottenham winger off to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-hyeok is in talks to join Belgian side Westerlo. The 20-year-old, who joined Spurs in 2025, has had loan spells with QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry City since. The South Korea international is expected in Belgium today for his medical.

Hammers knocked back in Parrott pursuit

West Ham have had their opening bid for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott rejected.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Hammers made their opening offer of around £15million over the weekend but it is likely to take a Championship record fee of £17.5m to get their man. They are now formulating a new offer.

RB Leipzig have also contacted Alkmaar in recent days but the Hammers are further advanced.

West Ham are exploring a move for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson and have made an approach for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Tigers turned down in Vipotnik chase

Hull have had a bid rejected by Swansea for striker Zan Vipotnik.

The Premier League side's offer is understood to have fallen well short of Swansea's valuation of last season's Championship top scorer.

Palace keen on Khalaili

Crystal Palace's move for Union Saint-Gilloise right wing-back Anan Khalaili is progressing.

The Israeli international saw a £21million move to Inter Milan collapse over a medical issue but has had a number of clubs enquiring since.

Khalaili has had his medical ahead of signing a five-year deal.

Charles edges closer to Fulham switch

Shea Charles is undergoing his Fulham medical this morning ahead of his £30million transfer from Southampton.

Fulham have agreed to pay £27m with a further £3m in add-ons for the 22-year-old after Manchester City declined their option to activate matching rights.

Southampton retain a 20 per cent sell-on while Charles has agreed a five-year deal with an option for a further year.

McNeil and Johnson undergo medicals

Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson have undergone medicals and agreed four-year contracts ahead of their swap move to Crystal Palace and Everton respectively.

The clubs say no fees are involved despite McNeil having only one year left on contract and Johnson having four.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

McNeil nearly joined Palace on Deadline Day in January, but the £20m move broke down due to paperwork not being submitted in time.

Johnson has struggled to settle at Palace since joining from Tottenham for £35m in January. Everton have also held an interest in Johnson in previous windows.

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

Hammers approach Vardy

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

Leicester have signed goalkeeper Franco Ravizzoli on a free transfer from Blackpool.

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Araujo completes medical

Ronald Araujo has completed his Liverpool medical ahead of completing a loan move from Barcelona.

The 27-year-old's signing is expected to be announced this afternoon.

The Uruguay defender's loan also includes an option to buy for around £47.1m.

Villa keep tabs on Endrick

Aston Villa are among the growing list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid. The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024.

Read the full story here.

Masuaku closes on Turkey move

Sunderland defender Arthur Masuaku is finalising finalise his move to Konyaspor, in Turkey. A deal between the clubs was agreed over the weekend.

Masuaku joined Sunderland last summer and spent the second half of last season on loan at Lens.

Belgian club Mechelen have agreed a deal to sign Sunderland defender Leo Hjelde.

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

Sunderland are interested in signing Alex Palmer from Ipswich

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side with Anthony Patterson expected to undergo a medical at Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee around £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Sunderland face Ipswich on the opening day of the season.

Ipswich are among the clubs interested in Newcastle's Nick Pope.

Villa on hunt for MacPhee replacement

Burnley set-piece coach Pal Fjelde is in talks to join Aston Villa.

Villa lost Austin MacPhee to Chelsea last month and 32-year-old Fjelde would be his replacement.

Fjelde joined Burnley last year and has also been his home country of Norway’s set piece coach since June 2022.

Austin MacPhee (right) left Villa to join Chelsea this summer

As a player he was a defender and midfielder and played for Norwegian clubs Viking and Bryne, before brief spells with Scottish Premiership side St Mirren and Faroe Islands Premier League side 07 Vestur.

Sports.content:
Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, has also become a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Villa director of football Damian Vidagany told German outlet Bild: 'Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans. We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.'

Talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the Newcastle deal

They have also missed out on top targets including Spain winger Victor Munoz, who opted to join Liverpool

Villa lost 2-1 to Bayern in a pre-season friendly in Hong Kong over the weekend and Palhinha came on as a substitute.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, star forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, the manager who saved them from relegation before transforming them into a Champions League club and their 56-year major trophy drought, then stepped down on July 31.

They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

Howe has since been replaced by a Jaissle, who joins from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli. The 38-year-old's previous coaching experiences include a two-year spell at RB Salzburg preceded by a short-term stint at Austrian side Liefering.

They have recouped north of £250million following the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and have made five signings this summer - goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal and have also lost key players in Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon too

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup second-round draw: Chelsea host League One Luton, Tottenham handed London derby and Fulham welcome neighbours AFC Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup second-round draw: Chelsea host League One Luton, Tottenham handed London derby and Fulham welcome neighbours AFC Wimbledon

New manager Xabi Alonso will begin the club's bid to win the competition for the first time since 2015 later this month.

Eleven Premier League clubs have entered at the second-round stage, with those involved in European competition this season receiving a bye to the third round.
