Sports.title: Crystal Palace hold clear-the-air talks with Dwight McNeil's girlfriend ahead of imminent transfer - after she hit out at club over failed January move
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace co-owner and chairman Steve Parish has moved to clear the air with Dwight McNeil's partner ahead of the Everton player's imminent move to the club, according to reports.

McNeil and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deals. But this isn't the first time McNeil was primed for a move to the Eagles - having nearly joined them on Deadline Day in January.

The Everton winger, 26, had been widely expected to complete a move to the south London club after undergoing a medical ahead of a loan deal with a £20million obligation to buy.

The Eagles had submitted a deal sheet for McNeil's move, but they then failed to complete the relevant paperwork in time.

Everton sources said they fulfilled their part but Palace went quiet on finalising paperwork, effectively pulling out, and the transfer ran out of time.

And Megan Sharpley, girlfriend of McNeil, took to Instagram in a lengthy series of stories to hit out at what went on, including accusing Palace of messing with McNeil's mental health.

In a searing statement she described the 'cruelty' of the football world, saying that McNeil had been 'toyed with until the final minute' and subsequently 'left broken hearted with nothing but confusion'.

McNeil and Crystal Palace's Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deals to Everton and Palace

In February, Dwight McNeil's girlfriend had hit out at the 'cruel' world of football after his deadline day move to Crystal Palace collapsed at the last moment

Sharpley also revealed that McNeil was left 'distressed' and in tears after the move fell through

Now, according to The Times, Parish has reached out to Sharpley to smooth things over so the transfer can move ahead. Both McNeil and Johnson spent Monday having medicals, with four-year deals for both players having been prepared.

As for the original statement, Sharpley said: 'Dwight, I've always been in awe of your job,' she began. 'The way you've committed most of your life to achieve what only the 0.1 per cent achieve.

'I know you love your job, the sport and you know how lucky you are to do what most people only dream of.

'We appreciate our lives, how fortunate we are, and the millions of football fans that keep the game alive and ultimately keep you in a job you adore. You've sacrificed a lot and most people don't have much of an idea of the difficult hardships you've suffered and dealt with in your personal life. And we crack on, that's who we are, we appreciate how blessed our lives are.

'But the world doesn't seem to accept that someone as fortunate as you is allowed to suffer hardships and feel sad. But you're a human, a beautiful incredible 26-year-old human being. And no matter about money or the success you've worked so hard to achieve, you are allowed to feel.

'Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you.'

Sharpley continued: 'To have something promised to you, to have been dragged along on an emotional rollercoaster, and to be toyed with until the final minute.

'To have 4-and-a-half-years of your life promised to you, traveling, medicals, agreements made... promises made. To have prepared to move your entire life, our life 100 of miles away in the space of a few hours.

'For it to be torn away from you at the last second, with absolutely no explanation. Going from everything - to radio silence, no phone call, no communication and be left, broken hearted with nothing but confusion, has hurt more than I can say.

'I sit with you, knowing in my heart and deep down into my soul that you will bounce back from this. I am your biggest supporter. And I know you will overcome this with a fire in your belly and a motivation that no one can stop. I have already seen it tonight, even whilst you're facing the lowest point of your career.'

Sharpley reaffirmed her support for her partner and revealed he had been left in tears by the collapse of the transfer.

After the lengthy series of Instagram stories from Sharpley, McNeil also spoke on the matter

'We live in a world where everyone is aware how big of a problem mental health is,' she added. 'So in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money, that it's okay to mess and toy with their mental health and that's just 'part of the job'?

'No matter of money, we all deserve to be treated with respect, kindness and fairly. So I really question the industry tonight. I only hope there's more done in the future to protect people from situations like what I've witnessed tonight.

'Football is brutal and yes, it's the nature of the beast, but messing with human beings feelings and emotions shouldn't be acceptable. People only see one side on the media, you don't see the tears, the emotion and the distress I've seen tonight.

'Dwight, to the present, and the future. Every single thing happens for a reason, I will always believe what is meant for you will find you, and with your hard work and determination I'll never doubt only the best will come your way, and I'm so excited to see what you can achieve...

'So here's to carrying on being an Everton player. The support we've had from this club, especially during my illness, has meant a lot on our journey, so let's keep grinding, keep working and grafting for this badge. Let's keep going Dwight, show them who you are. I'm right by your side.'

The emotional post from Sharpley referenced her own illness when she was diagnosed with a large, serious tumour on her ovary and was forced to undergo urgent open surgery in December 2023. McNeil was praised for his unwavering support at the time.

The winger, who has played 128 times for Everton since joining from Burnley in 2022, also weighed in on the situation in regards to his failed move.

Sharing the final story from his partner, McNeil added: 'Whilst even now I'm still left in the dark. What I do know, and have been supported with, I am an Everton player. I will use this as motivation.

'I love you moo, I couldn't thank you enough for all of your love and support.'

Sports.title: Cristian Romero moves closer to sealing £34m move to Atletico Madrid with Diego Simeone on the cusp of seeing off Arsenal, Inter and Barcelona for Spurs captain
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid are moving closer to agreement with Tottenham over a £34million deal to sign Cristian Romero.

The clubs are still understood to be a few million apart on the fixed aspect of the fee and bonus structure still need to be decided.

Atletico with the pull of coach Diego Simeone are understood to be Romero's preference over the other clubs that have been involved.

The Argentine has been the subject of interest from Inter Milan, Spurs' fierce rivals Arsenal and Barcelona.

Atletico are in the throes of selling defender Nahuel Molina to Roma, and he has arrived in Italy ahead of completing his £14.5m move, while Aston Villa are finalising a £16m deal for Atletico left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

Daily Mail Sport understands Premier League champions Arsenal had contacted the agents of the Spurs captain over what the deal would be, but Tottenham are unaware of the Gunners' interest and would be unwilling to consider selling 28-year-old Romero to their north London rivals.

Cristian Romero is moving closer to sealing a £34m move to Spanish side Atletico Madrid

Daily Mail Sport understands the pull of Diego Simeone has seen Atletico lead the race

Inter have agreed a £34m fee with Spurs but have not agreed on personal terms.

The central defender is free to leave Spurs for the right price after the club bolstered their defensive ranks earlier in the transfer window.

The additions of Marcos Senesi on a free transfer and John Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52m mean Roberto de Zerbi is well stocked.

But the idea of selling the club captain to their arch rivals Arsenal would be deemed completely unacceptable by Spurs fans and the club would not countenance it.

Arsenal will be without William Saliba, who suffered a back injury at the World Cup, for months and are considering reinforcements at the back.

But Romero appears destined for a move away from the Premier League having spent the last five years at Tottenham after joining from Atalanta.

He was at the heart of Lionel Scaloni's defence for the Argentina side who beat England in the World Cup semi-final before suffering a 1-0 defeat by Spain in the final last month.

Romero has come close to leaving Spurs before, notably after Ange Postecoglou departed.

He suffered a knee injury during the club's dramatic run-in at the end of last season in which they fought off relegation.

Romero left the pitch in tears during a 1-0 defeat by Sunderland but De Zerbi managed to keep Spurs up without his captain, who recovered in time to play for Argentina.

He came under fire for celebrating in the faces of opposition players during the World Cup and also snubbed Donald Trump after the final defeat, ignoring the US President after collecting his runners-up medal.

After receiving his medal around his neck from Infantino, Romero snubbed Trump by not shaking his hand, instead he walked straight past him to join his team-mates.

Sports.title: Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle
Sports.content:
Liverpool confirm the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola moves to fix defensive crisis just 13 days out from Premier League opener against Newcastle

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan with an option to buy.

The 27-year-old defender flew to Merseyside on Sunday afternoon and has since completed his medical.

The Reds have the option to purchase the Uruguay international at the end of the campaign for £47million.

'I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy,' Araujo said.

'I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my teammates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

'I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

'As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time.'

Liverpool have confirmed the loan signing of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo

The Uruguayan defender has joined the Anfield club on a season long loan

Andoni Iraola has sought to address his defensive crisis with a number of centre halves injured

Araujo wanted to leave Barca, where he has spent eight years, after talks with coach Hansi Flick made it apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts. He believes he is likely to play more minutes under Reds' new boss Andoni Iraola.

The centre-back gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at the heart of the backline and at right-back.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre-back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, and new signing Jeremy Jacquet is yet to feature this summer.

It leaves captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully fit senior centre-back with their Premier League opener away at Newcastle less than two weeks away.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2020.

He has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona but finds himself down the pecking order in Spain, with the likes of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin ahead of him.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner

Evangelos Marinakis has filed a claim for defamation at the High Court over a banner unfurled by Crystal Palace supporters which depicted him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White's head

View 2 Images Evangelos Marinakis has brought a claim against Crystal Palace (Image: Nicolas Koutsokostas/Getty Images)

Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace over a banner which showed him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White's head.

‌



Lawyers for the Greek shipping magnate filed the claim for defamation at the High Court on Monday. The filing is against CPFC Limited, the commercial entity of Crystal Palace, and "Persons Unknown".

‌



It comes almost a year after the banner was shown by Palace supporters during the 1-1 draw between the two clubs at Selhurst Park on August 24 in the Premier League.

‌



The banner read: "Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption."

Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has never been charged with any of the stated offences. Palace refused to comment when contacted by Mirror Football, while Forest didn't respond.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Carabao Cup second round draw in full as Chelsea, Newcastle and Leeds discover opponents READ MORE :

Palace were charged by the Football Association with misconduct in November over the banner. They were alleged to have failed to ensure that supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or provocative way.

‌



In February, the FA fined Palace £50,000 over the incident. The ruling noted: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

The banner came shortly after Forest held onto star player Gibbs-White following interest from Tottenham. Spurs were understood to have triggered the midfielder's £60million release clause, only for him to then sign a new contract with Forest.

View 2 Images Morgan Gibbs-White with Evangelos Marinakis (Image: Nottingham Forest FC)

‌



Gibbs-White then did a video interview alongside Marinakis in which he explained his decision to stay put. "I've felt at home at Forest from the moment I arrived," he said at the time. "The support from the fans, my team-mates, and everyone around the club has been unbelievable.

"I believe in what we're building here – and with the backing of [owner] Mr Marinakis and the enormous ambition he has, I want to be part of making something special. I'm excited for what's to come."

Marinakis added: "There was significant interest from various clubs, but we were determined to build our future with Morgan at the heart of it. I promised our fans we would not only compete, but grow stronger and stronger every season. Today is another big step in that journey."

Article continues below

There has been heightened tensions between Palace and Forest over the past year after the London side lost their place in the Europa League. Palace qualified by winning the FA Cup in 2025, only to be ejected by UEFA, who found they had broken third-party ownership rules.

Forest ended up taking their place in UEFA's second cup competition, with Palace demoted to the Conference League, which they ended up winning anyway under the management of Oliver Glasner. Glasner left Palace at the end of last season and has now taken over as Forest's manager, working under Marinakis.

Sports.title: What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture
Sports.content:
What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture

Marcus Rashford's future remains the topic of plenty of speculation as he returns to Manchester United after spending last season out on loan

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has rejoined his Manchester United team-mates after a spell out on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

A few months ago, the idea of Marcus Rashford returning to the fold at Manchester United looked far-fetched. Strange things can happen in football, though, and the England international's Old Trafford comeback is right up there

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and looked poised for a permanent move to Spotify Camp Nou. However, the Catalan club let their £26m option expire.

‌



For as long as Ruben Amorim was in the United dugout, a return for the forward looked impossible. However, the arrival of Michael Carrick - a former team-mate of Rashford - has altered the picture.

‌



England's run to the World Cup semi-finals meant a later return for the 28-year-old than for some of his colleagues. Now, though, Rashford's future is very much at the forefront of discussions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Man Utd return

Following United's 1-1 draw with PSG on Saturday, Carrick confirmed that Rashford has returned as part of his first team group, alongside Kobbie Mainoo.

‌



“We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together," United's manager said. “Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

View 3 Images Rashford has joined the United camp in Dublin (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Manchester United have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, i nspired by the club's heritage and featuring a classic polo collar with iconic adidas details.

‌



As reported by the MEN, the England pair joined Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt, Karl Darlow, JJ Gabriel and Tynan Thompson on a private jet to Dublin. Some of those players could play a part in United's midweek friendly with Leeds, with Martinez also expected in Dublin.

Transfer stance

Rashford is not interested in moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia, thereby limiting his options. He would only join a European side who can offer him Champions League football. There are only so many clubs capable of meeting the forward's demands and one of them, Barcelona, are already out of the running barring a big U-turn.

The fee might not be a huge obstacle, with the MEN suggesting £25m - a little less than the provisional sum agreed with Barca - potentially enough to do it. However, those close to Rashford are said to have suggested United are no longer desperate to sell.

‌



Rashford will be with the rest of the squad for United's final two pre-season friendlies, against Leeds on Wednesday and AC Milan on Saturday, and is expected to be around for the Premier League opener away at Hull on August 22.

View 3 Images Barcelona allowed their £26m transfer option to expire (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer/Getty Images)

Telling gesture

While some fans are prepared to wait and see when it comes to Rashford's future, others have been looking for clues wherever they can find them. One such clue comes on the squad number front, where the forward is set to wear No. 14 next term.

Article continues below

United have already given Matheus Cunha the No. 10 previously worn by the England international and there are no indications it will revert back to its previous owner. Rashford wore No. 14 at Barcelona, though, and the choice can be read as an indication that the club and Carrick consider him part of their plans.

The No. 14 shirt was vacant for United last season. The number was not reused when Christian Eriksen left the club, while previous holders include Jesse Lingard and Javier Hernandez.

Sports.title: Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title
Sports.content:
Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title

Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month

View Image Oleksandr Khyzhniak is a rising star

Oleksandr Khyzhniak, who many believe can follow in mentor Oleksandr Usyk's footsteps, will fight for his first title later this month.

‌



Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month. He will now headline the second boxing event put on by Usyk's promotional company Usyk 17 Promotions on August 22.

‌



The event, to be held at !FESTrepublic in Lviv, will be dedicated to the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence and Usyk said: “Thirty-five years of independent development is actually not a very long time. Twelve of those years have been lived under conditions of war. But look at how much we have already managed to achieve despite everything.

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

"Look at the incredible athletes we have — not only boxers, but Olympic champions and Paralympians. Artists, musicians, scientists. We want to remember our greatest victories, honour those who fought and continue to fight for our freedom, and show the entire world that Ukraine has been, is and will remain a country of strong, talented and unbreakable people.”

Sergey Lapin, who is guiding Khyzhniak in his professional career, added:“A first title fight is both a natural and an important step in Oleksandr’s professional career. He is ready for a new level of competition and to prove his quality in championship fights. For Usyk 17 Promotions, it is especially important that this stage of his journey begins in Ukraine — at our second boxing event in Lviv. Our goal is to build a platform in Ukraine where the strongest boxers can develop, win titles and confidently progress to the international level.”

Article continues below

The fight night's co-main event will feature Pavlo Illiusha while the undercard will include nine Usyk 17 Promotions boxers in Maksym Rudyk, Maksym Zymenko, Dmytro Lovchynskyi, Elvin Aliiev, Bohdan Tolmachov, Mykola Laktionov, Jamal Kuliev, Aider Abduraimov and Matvii Razhba.

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment

Billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is involved in a consortium looking to buy into Liverpool with a statement anticipated soon

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium looking to take a stake in Liverpool (Image: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue)

Jeff Bezos is preparing to take a stake in Liverpool. The billionaire is part of a consortium which also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

‌



Amazon founder Bezos has been one of the richest men in the world for a number of years. He sat fourth on the most recent Forbes billionaires list, with his fortune now estimated to sit at $280bn (just under £208m).

‌



According to Sky News, an official announcement over the deal could arrive this week. The consortium is reportedly led by Amit Bhatia, the former QPR chairman and son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

‌



An investment in Liverpool would just be the latest step for the super-rich businessman, who boasts a huge property empire along with wife Lauren Sanchez. Here, we've taken a deeper dive into what that looks like.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Reports from Realtor.com estimates Bezos' property empire to be worth some $500m (£370m) on its own. The star of the show is his primary home on Indian Creek Island in Florida, an exclusive island with just 34 residences - unsurprisingly belonging to the super-rich.

Three of those belong to Bezos, including a $90m property bought in 2024. While the size of the home means he might not have neighbours in the same sense as you or I, other residents of Indian Creek Island include NFL legend Tom Brady and first daughter Ivanka Trump.

Previously, Bezos lived in Seattle with his former wife Mackenzie Scott and still owns a number of properties in the area. He made a tidy profit on one of his homes in the small town of Hunts Point, buying for $37.5m in 2019 and selling for $63m four years later, per the Puget Sound Business Journal.

‌



View 3 Images Bezos owns property on the exclusive Indian Creek Island (Image: Google Maps)

Get Liverpool's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 LFC Shop Buy Now on LFC Shop Product Description Liverpool FC have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27, inspired by iconic adidas strip worn during the club's 1989/90 title-winning campaign.

The 62-year-old established Amazon in Washington State in the 90s and also purchased properties in the Seattle suburb of Medina. He isn't the only Hunts Point resident with ties to Seattle, with former Seattle Seahawks NFL coach Pete Carroll among the others to buy property there.

‌



Over the last decade, Bezos has also picked up properties in Washington DC and New York City, each worth more than $15m, and a ranch in West Texas. That's nothing compared to his $78m Hawaii property, though, which is believed to include a 4,500-square-foot main house.

However, it's a $165m Beverly Hills home which tops the lot. The California property was developed by movie mogul Jack Warner and previously belonged to record executive David Geffen, with Architectural Digest reporting that it includes tennis courts and its own nine-hole golf course.

View 3 Images Bezos and wife Lauren Sanchez also own properties in Texas and California worth millions of dollars (Image: Google Maps)

‌



It isn't just about property for Bezos either. The bulk of his wealth still comes from his Amazon stake, despite him selling shares worth a reported $13.5bn in 2023, while he has a private investment firm - Bezos Expeditions - which manages his other investments.

These investments include stakes in Uber and Airbnb, among other ventures, with the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute estimating Bezos investments has approximately $107.8bn of assets. The billionaire also took charge of the Washington Post more than a decade ago in a deal worth $250m.

Another significant project of Bezos is Blue Origin, the space technology company he established in 2000. The company, which produces rockets and engines, was described in 2023 by CEO Bob Smith as having "hundreds of millions in revenue as well as billions of dollars in orders".

Article continues below

While Bezos is one of the richest individuals in the world, fellow consortium member Saverin is reportedly worth nearly $24bn himself. The 44-year-old is a co-founder of venture capital firm B Capital and is now based in Singapore.

Sky News reports that the bid values Liverpool at around $6bn. The club was valued at $4.5bn when Dynasty Equity took a small stake in 2023, though the Bezos-Saverin consortium could take a stake of more than 30 per cent.

Sports.title: Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting
Sports.content:
Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting

Arsenal are firm admirers of Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, and they are looking at potentially signing the ex-Manchester City star after missing out on Vinicius Junior

View Image Julian Alvarez has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez will reportedly push to leave Atletico Madrid this summer, with Arsenal keen on landing the Argentinian. It's claimed, though, the 26-year-old will reiterate his desire to join Barcelona, having previously said it would be his dream to move to the Nou Camp.

‌



Alvarez is due to return for pre-season training this week, with Arsenal keeping a close eye on developments. Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has been a long-term admirer of the former Manchester City forward, who has racked up 49 goals and 17 assists in 106 appearances for Atletico.

‌



However, the La Liga giants club have stood firm with their stance that Alvarez is not for sale, even after his controversial comments during the World Cup.

‌



Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move READ MORE :

Arsenal outline Gabriel Martinelli transfer stance as new club eyes Gabriel Jesus READ MORE :

"I spoke with people at the club, with those I had to speak with and the best thing for everyone is ‌a transfer and I want to fulfil my dream," he said.

"It's not the time to talk about this, but I also can't hide ⁠it. I try to ⁠be an honest person."

‌



Alvarez has been the subject of bids from both Barcelona and Real Madrid, yet his manager Diego Simeone maintains that nothing has shifted and that Atletico have no plans to sanction his exit.

"The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel Gil Marin [Atletico's CEO] explained very well," Simeone said. "We are very happy with Julian, from a sporting perspective, we're very happy to have a player like Julian, and we'll help him continue to grow and improve."

Ahead of his return to Atleti, Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Alvarez will once again make his desire to join Barcelona abundantly clear, despite having already expressed this both privately and publicly, as the saga enters its 'decisive phase'.

‌



This would strongly suggest that Arsenal would be out of the running for his signature should the Spanish giants alter their position.

Atleti have remained resolute thus far, though the Argentine continues to harbour hopes that the club might eventually have a change of heart. The publication warns that 'a major crisis could erupt' between Atleti and the Argentine.

‌



It is further reported that should Atletico ease their stance and agree to open talks, Barcelona 'will submit a new offer'.

Nevertheless, Gil Marin has left no doubt that the club will not be entertaining any offers for their prized asset this summer.

"It wasn't the right day to make such statements; it was a day for [Lionel] Messi and the Argentine national team, not Julian," he previously told EFE about Alvarez's comments regarding his desire to leave.

Article continues below

"Julian has a dream [to sign elsewhere], but we Atletico fans have dreams, too. It is true that he has spoken to us, but it is also true that he is fully aware of our position because we have been very clear. Atleti do not want to transfer him. He is a great player and we are very proud that he plays for us."

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star claims he's been told Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star claims he's been told Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'

Bradley Barcola is a target for both Liverpool and Arsenal amid his uncertain future at Paris Saint-Germain, and the Gunners are said to have the upper hand on their Premier League rivals

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is a wanted man (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Ex-Arsenal forward Perry Groves says he's been told that Gunners target Bradley Barcola 'wants to live in London'. Barcola, 23, is hot property this summer, with Liverpool already in talks with Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



PSG's lofty demand of £145million has put the breaks on a move, leaving his future uncertain with three weeks to go until transfer deadline day. The Frenchman returned to training with Luis Enrique's side on Monday but is open to a move.

‌



Arsenal have already missed out on two wingers this summer, Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers, and have been tipped to go for Barcola as an alternative. And Groves' claim suggests that his old club boast an advantage over Liverpool.

‌



The former Gunners man, who played for the club between 1986 and 1992, told talkSPORT: "I've got a source that says he wants to live in London. I can't tell you [who], I can't divulge my sources. I've got a source. I've got a mole. Barcola wants to live in London."

But location isn't the only factor in Arsenal's favour, Groves added. "I've got no dog in the fight, but I would say the Gooners because Liverpool are a team that are in transition" he continued.

‌



"Andoni Iraola going in there, imposing his own philosophy, his own style with all the new signings coming in. If you were Barcola and you thought, what out of those two sides have got the most chance of winning the Premier League or Champions League, at the moment you'd say it was Arsenal.

"So it's whether Arsenal want to go in, if they go in for him, then there would have been advances being made to his people. Because they don't want to be seen losing out on Vinicius Junior being played like a little kitten with a ball of wool, but Arsenal have to be in for those sorts of players. That's the level Arsenal are at now."

Who should Bradley Barcola sign for - Arsenal or Liverpool? Have your say in the comments section.

"It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very much looking forward to that.

Sports.title: Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move
Sports.content:
Arsenal open transfer talks over next deal but major hurdle could stop record move

Arsenal are in talks with Galatasaray over a potential deal for Gabriel Martinelli, who is into the final 12 months of his contract at the Emirates Stadium

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal in the summer transfer window (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal and Galatasaray are in talks over a possible move for Gabriel Martinelli.

‌



Martinelli, 25, has entered the final 12 months of his contract at the Emirates Stadium and lost his spot in the starting XI to Leandro Trossard last season. While Trossard has since departed to join Besiktas, Christos Tzolis has arrived in a £34million deal from Club Brugge and the Gunners remain in the market for a new left winger.

‌



This has left Martinelli's future hanging in the balance, with speculation suggesting he could leave before the transfer window closes. Now, according to football.london, Arsenal are in negotiations with Galatasaray over a fee for the Brazilian, following an enquiry from the Turkish Super Lig side on the weekend.

‌



Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss READ MORE :

OPINION Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat by Ryan Taylor

However, no deal will be approved until there is progress in the opposite direction and Arsenal secure a left wing signing themselves, having missed out on Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

Tzolis has been Arsenal's first-choice on the left flank during pre-season, finding the net against Girona on his debut before providing an assist from a corner against Real Betis. He subsequently set up the Gunners' second goal in their 3-2 loss to Borussia Dortmund on Sunday and is proving to be a genuine threat down that side.

‌



Martinelli, meanwhile, was absent from Arsenal's opening pre-season fixture at Girona but has since come off the bench as a second-half substitute against Betis and Dortmund. He appeared for the final 12 minutes in the defeat to the German side and netted in the subsequent Emirates Cup penalty shootout.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli could be sold by Arsenal before the end of the summer window (Image: PA)

Speaking after the Dortmund match, Arteta confirmed the Gunners remain busy in the transfer market as they look to bolster their ranks. "Well, that's what we're trying to do (sign more players)," the Spaniard said. "It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very much looking forward to that."

‌



Arsenal snapped up Martinelli for just £6m back in 2019 and he has since gone on to make 278 appearances for the Gunners, netting 62 goals. However, he struggled to make any real impression last season, losing his regular starting berth to Trossard.

Belgian international Trossard delivered several standout moments for Mikel Arteta's side on the road to the Premier League title, before being offloaded for £15.3m to Besiktas. Martinelli could follow his team-mate with a switch to Turkish top-flight rivals Galatasaray, albeit for a considerably larger transfer fee.

While no precise transfer figure has been suggested for Martinelli, his age and profile would undoubtedly command a higher price than what Besiktas forked out for Trossard. Galatasaray are also said to be in discussions with AC Milan regarding a transfer for winger Rafael Leao, with a £43m price tag under consideration.

Article continues below

Should Arsenal secure a comparable sum for Martinelli, it would surpass the club's existing record sale, which saw Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain join Liverpool for £35m back in 2019.

Sports.title: Liverpool set to announce new signing but team-mate 'already wants him back' after goodbyes
Sports.content:
Liverpool set to announce new signing but team-mate 'already wants him back' after goodbyes

Ronald Araujo is poised to join Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona, but one team-mate is gutted to be losing his pal this month, and hopes to see him return next year

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo is set to sign for Liverpool on a season-long loan. (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ronald Araujo is already wanted back at Barcelona, despite his transfer to Liverpool not yet being officially confirmed. The defender is set to sign a season-long loan with the Reds.

‌



The arrival of the Uruguay international will ease some of the defensive worries that Andoni Iraola may have as the club builds up to the Premier League season opener against Newcastle United in under two weeks' time. The 27-year-old can play as a central defender or right-back.

‌



Liverpool will have a £47 million option to make the transfer permanent next summer if the loan spell goes well. But, Araujo's Barcelona team-mate Fermin Lopez is hoping that's not the case.

‌

"It's a shame, because he's a captain and I have a good relationship with him. He made the decision to continue developing and I hope he comes back next season."

Araujo has spent the past eight years at Barcelona and has worn the captain's armband at the Nou Camp since being appointed to the role in January.

‌



View 2 Images Fermin Lopez is sad to see his Barcelona team-mate go (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Yet he struggled to nail down a regular starting berth, managing just 16 starts last season — a campaign during which he stepped away from the game for mental health reasons. Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has shed light on his decision to allow the defender to depart this summer.

"I think Ronald is a great guy and a fantastic player," he said.

"I think our style of play, that we want to play, is a little bit different. He's a player that has a lot of speed, he's physical and very strong and also with the ball he's quite good.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania

Final: Ukraine/Sweden vs Poland/Albania

Play-off Path C:

Semi-final: Turkey vs Romania

Semi-final: Slovakia vs Kosovo

Final: Slovakia/Kosovo vs Turkey/Romania

Play-off Path D:

Semi-final: Denmark vs North Macedonia

Semi-final: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland

Final: Czech Republic/Republic of Ireland vs Denmark/North Macedonia - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL: Frank Warren talks up new golden age of British heavyweight boxing as prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for Filip Hrgovic showdown
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL: Frank Warren talks up new golden age of British heavyweight boxing as prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for Filip Hrgovic showdown

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Frank Warren has signalled a new ‘golden age' for British heavyweight boxing as his prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic at London’s O2 on August 29.

The 21-year-old Itauma was already set to face the 31-year-old Croatian in a championship eliminator when the fight was promoted into a battle for the IBF title after undisputed heavyweight king Oleksandr Usyk vacated all four alpha-belts.

Hrgovic’s only defeat in 21 fights came when he was knocked out in the eighth round two years ago by Daniel Dubois, who went on to become the WBO champion by stopping Fabio Wardley in a bloodied slugfest this May. Those two Englishmen will meet again in a rematch in October.

Hall of Fame Promoter Warren also has in his stable Tyson Fury who is heading for his long, long awaited Battle of Britain with Anthony Joshua in November at either Wembley Stadium or New York’s fabled Madison Square Garden.

‘These are amazingly exciting times for heavyweight boxing in this country,’ says Warren. ‘We have a whole programme of mouth-watering fights pencilled in our calendar at Queensberry.

'Although Moses is in his toughest fight yet I expect him to become the second youngest ever world heavyweight champion behind Mike Tyson.

Moses Itauma is preparing for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic

‘He would then have to deal with a mandatory defence against (American) Frank Mitchell, who I don’t think is as talented as Hrgovic.

'Win that and we should be looking at an IBF - WBO title unification fight between him and the winner of Dubois v Wardley. All of those are huge punchers and that fight would sell-out Wembley in a heart-beat.’

All the above are on Queensberry's books except Mitchell and Joshua and Warren says: ‘I expect Tyson to beat AJ on seniors night and quite possibly carry on to fight whichever of the young bloods comes out on top as the new undisputed heavyweight champion.

‘Imagine Itauma the hottest most talked about heavy on the planet against Fury the box office Gypsy King.

'Is there a stadium big enough for that.By the last Saturday night this month the UK will know for sure what Itauma is all about. And as it happens even at his age he has the maturity and the level head to carry it all off. Even though every fight in his sights now will be as dangerous as they come.

‘Buckle up.'

Sports.title: Heavyweight boxer Joseph Parker is CLEARED of doping after proving positive drugs test was caused by exposure to his nutritionist taking cocaine
Sports.content:
Heavyweight boxer Joseph Parker is CLEARED of doping after proving positive drugs test was caused by exposure to his nutritionist taking cocaine

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ex-heavyweight boxing champion Joseph Parker has been cleared of breaking drug rules after proving his adverse test finding was due to his nutritionist taking cocaine.

Parker, 34, was found to have traces of the Class A drug in his system on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley last October following a test conducted by the Voluntary Anti-Doping Agency (VADA).

He denied knowingly taking the substance and a UK Anti-Doping (UKAD) investigation has now ruled in his favour, saying the boxer provided enough evidence to back up his argument that his positive test was due to exposure to cocaine taken by his nutritionist.

Parker was suspended for three months before that ban was lifted in June when UKAD determined that the ingestion of cocaine metabolite benzoylecgonine took place out of competition and was 'in a context unrelated to sport performance'.

The New Zealander is now free to fight again and could compete twice before the end of the year, according to his manager.

UKAD said: 'On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the adverse analytical finding was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

Joseph Parker's positive test was due to exposure to his nutritionist's cocaine, UKAD found

'The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout.'

Parker himself wrote on his social media channels: 'I'm pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I'll be back in the ring soon.

'I've been advised to say no more for now while details are finalised. Thank you to all my supporters.'

Parker has been a regular at the top of the heavyweight division over the last decade, winning the WBO world title in 2016 before losing it against Anthony Joshua two years later in Cardiff.

He will be looking to improve his record of 36 wins and four defeats and his manager, David Higgins, believes the best is yet to come, saying Parker is 'relieved and excited' by the outcome of the investigation.

He told Sky Sports: 'Joseph is champing at the bit to get back into the ring. He was up early to go for a run this morning.

'He feels like he is at the peak of his powers and they say a heavyweight only reaches his prime in his thirties. Joseph is only 34 and if you look at the names on his resume, you could call him a veteran but he's still relatively young.
